News.title: Shocking moment fire breaks out on luxury 30ft boat after explosion on board sparked huge trail of smoke as 3 injured
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a boat is seen up in flames as thick plumes of choking smoke billow into the air.

Three people were rushed to hospital after a luxury 30ft vessel exploded off the coast of City Island in the Bronx and sparked a huge fireball.



The terrifying inferno unfolded at around 1.40pm.

Shocking footage shows flames raging across the body of the vessel as a thick column of black smoke spirals into the sky.



Two people can be seen hugging on the docks as they watch the terrifying scene.

Half of the hull collapsed and was destroyed in the blast as the sleek white vessel transformed into a blackened husk.



More than 70 firefighters from 21 units raced to the scene of the inferno.

Rescuers rushed three people to hospital with minor injuries.

The boat had been docked at 691 Bridge St. in City Island when it ignited from causes as yet unknown.

Firefighters battled the flames for nearly an hour.



Cops have launched a probe into the mystery explosion.

It comes as a horror blast ripped through a charter boat in Florida, hospitalising 15.

The vessel exploded in Biscayne Bay, a bustling tourist spot in Miami in May.



Two children were among the victims – with one being treated for 18 per cent burns which scorched his body.

An adult is also in hospital with burns covering roughly 30 per cent of his skin.

Last year a boat captain was arrested following the explosion of his vessel.

More than 20 of his passengers leapt into icy waters to escape the boat-turned-fireball.

News.title: Fury as Burnham agrees pay rises with train drivers to avoid embarrassing strikes on London to Manchester line
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has agreed above-inflation pay rises with train drivers to avoid embarrassing strikes on the London to Manchester line.

It is his first public sector pay deal since he set up No10 North in Manchester — where his ministers now routinely have to travel via Avanti West Coast services.



Burnham has referred to this as a “transfer of power” out of London.

Leaked union correspondence shows the PM signed off a 3.6 per cent deal for Aslef drivers who start on £70,000 a year.



Shadow Transport Secretary Richard Holden accused Labour of capitulating to the unions.

He told The Sunday Times: “Taxpayers are being asked to stump up millions simply to save Burnham’s blushes.”

“This is Labour paying more for less.

“And it’s passengers and taxpayers footing the bill.”

The pay deal represents a huge win for the Aslef union, whose drivers are also set to receive a £720 bonus simply for turning up to work on a fifth day of the working week.

It came after their refusal to work on the rest of the days forced cuts to 38 services this summer.



Ministers have separately offered LNER drivers on the east coast mainline a 12 per cent pay rise over the next four years.

As well as softer requirements for sick notes and non-attendance.

News.title: Secret honours ‘blacklist’ of 400 celebs who can’t get gongs over their tax affairs is revealed
News.content:
MORE than 400 public figures are on an honours “blacklist” due to their controversial tax affairs.

HMRC officials, asked to vet possible recipients of awards such as a knighthood or OBE, have put 33 in a “high risk” category, and judged another 377 to be “medium risk”.



An official transparency release showed that of the 410 total for the last 11 years, 135 high-profile people were placed in those categories in just the last two years.

It said: “The Honours and Appointments Secretariat may ask HMRC to advise about any potential risk posed to the Government and the Crown by honours candidates in respect of their tax affairs.



“Checks are requested on a proportionate basis, taking account of the level of the honour and individual’s profile.”

Last year Rory McIlroy was part of Europe’s victorious Ryder Cup team, won the US Masters, which completed his career grand slam, and was the first Sports Personality winner in almost a decade to miss out on an honour in the same year.

Reports said Whitehall sources compared the snub to that of Sir David Beckham, who finally received his knighthood last year.

There were no details regarding McIlroy’s omission, but earlier in his career, he was among thousands of wealthy individuals who put money into another scheme that ended up being challenged by the taxman.

A Government spokesperson said: “Our role is to provide a low, medium or high tax-risk assessment, when requested, to inform the honours process.

“The main honours committee takes into account the risk rating alongside other information to decide whether to recommend the award of an honour.”

News.title: Boy, 13, seriously injured in stabbing inside Taco Bell as two teens arrested after ‘25 young men ran in with knives’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TEEN ATTACK Boy, 13, seriously injured in stabbing inside Taco Bell as two teens arrested after ‘25 young men ran in with knives’

A 13-YEAR-OLD boy has been seriously injured in a stabbing at a Taco Bell with two teenagers arrested in connection to the shocking attack.

Officers raced to reports of a stabbing on Saturday evening in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, after one diner claimed a group of 25 youths stormed the fast-food restaurant.

The shocking incident took place shortly after 6pm on Riverside Walk as emergency services descended on the scene.



A 13-year-old boy was found near the toilets having sustained serious injuries as he was rushed to hospital.



His current condition is unknown.

Greater Manchester Police has now arrested two teenage boys on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article.

One man, who was with his wife and children, told Manchester Evening News how a group of “around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives”.

The group then went into the bathroom where he heard ” a load of crying and screaming”.

David Lane claimed: “That’s when the lad got stabbed.

“I grabbed a load of napkins and put pressure on the wound. It looked like he lost a lot of blood. It was a hectic scene.”

Images show the Taco Bell restaurant cordoned off with police tape as officers and ambulance crews descended on the scene.



The restaurant was closed on Saturday evening as Crime Scene Investigation officers were pictured outside.

Mr Lane said the incident was “horrific” and that his children “shouldn’t have to see that”.

“If it wasn’t for my actions, I think he would have died,” he added.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “We were called to reports of a stabbing at 6.09pm on Riverside Walk. Boy, 13, taken to hospital with serious injuries.

“Two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing.”



The Sun has contacted Taco Bell and North West Ambulance Service for comment.

News.title: Teen pupils, 17, 14 & 13 die after being swept out to sea while playing as boy, 12, pulled from water in dramatic rescue
News.content:
SEA TRAGEDY Teen pupils, 17, 14 & 13 die after being swept out to sea while playing as boy, 12, pulled from water in dramatic rescue

THREE teenagers have drowned after a desperate rescue attempt ended in tragedy when they were swept out to sea while playing on rocks.

Brothers Haruki Shitaebisu, 17, and Kensei, 13, and their friend Takahiro Takemoto, 14, were among four youngsters dragged into the deadly waters.

They were playing along the rocky coastline and started jumping into the water when two suddenly got into trouble.

Desperate to save them, the other two boys leaped in – only to be swept away themselves.





A fifth student who escaped the terrifying ordeal desperately called for help.

The horror unfolded off Ichikikushikino in Kagoshima Prefecture, southwestern Japan, at around 3.30pm on Friday.

Rescue teams managed to find a 12-year-old boy and pull him to safety by using a Coast Guard patrol vessel.

But the other three teens vanished beneath the waves, triggering a frantic search that continued into Saturday.



Two bodies were recovered from the sea on Saturday morning.

A third was found later that afternoon in a state of cardiopulmonary arrest and was confirmed dead.

The Coast Guard identified two of the dead as Haruki and Takemoto, while the identity of the third, most likely missing Kensei, was still being investigated.

Rough waves had been predicted for the area, although no wave warning or advisory had been issued for the coastal area of Ichikikushikino City.



The Coast Guard initially said the area was off-limits for swimming, but later corrected the information and said swimming is allowed there.

Another report said swimming is prohibited at the site.

It comes just after a Brit dad died after being swept away in a rip tide while swimming with his wife and three kids in Indonesia.

They were out swimming at Kerandangan Beach at around 3.30pm on Wednesday when the father was suddenly taken by a rip tide.

He was missing underwater for 18 minutes before being pulled unconscious from the waves.



His wife and three children survived the ordeal.

News.title: Growing business can bag Burnham a triple bullseye – it’s time for PM to hit the target
News.content:
‘Deluded’ PM must listen to business

ANDY BURNHAM’S honeymoon is well and truly over.

On Tuesday he will finally have to stand up in Parliament and tell MPs what his plans really are.



The weeks of carefully placed soundbites and soft policy initiatives will finally be met with the hard reality of hostile questioning.

It is time for some straight talking, particularly on the economy.



Last week Mr Burnham was making sympathetic noises to the business community.

He has indicated that helping firms will be one of the big themes when he addresses MPs.

The PM said he was “acutely conscious” of how hard the trading environment is on the High Street and vowed: “I’m trying to make life easier.”

But it all sounds like classic Burnhamism.

Warm words to lift expectations tempered by the “challenging” fiscal backdrop.

His predecessor Sir Keir Starmer liked to call this “realistic hope”. And look where that got him.



If the PM really wants to help he must cut business taxes and lower the cost of creating jobs.

But don’t just take our word for it, Mr Burnham. Listen to the people who actually run big firms.

Mike Ashley employs 30,000 people. He calls the PM’s ideas on reviving the High Street “delusional”.

Lord Stuart Rose was boss of Marks and Spencer, which employs 65,000 people. He called Mr Burnham’s plans “a lot of b******s”.

And today Lord Richard Walker, chairman of the Iceland supermarket which employs almost 30,000, has a direct message: “Make it cheaper to employ people, invest and grow.”



If Mr Burnham wants to help employers he must listen to their critical voices.

Growing business not only boosts the economy, it also gets Neets into work and lowers the welfare bill.

That’s a triple bullseye.

Make sure you hit the target, PM.

We’ve hit a brick wall

RUINOUS energy costs don’t just wreck family budgets.



They also hold back our industry.

Construction experts say British-made bricks are now so expensive that it is cheaper to buy them from Europe.

Last year we imported a staggering 352million.

This crushing energy price burden is stifling firms and jobs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As he plans his budget, Andy Burnham should remember one thing:



You can’t build a better Britain if it is all made from foreign bricks.

News.title: Moment driver, 34, leads cops on 130mph police chase while high on cocaine & cannabis before getting stuck in traffic
News.content:
THIS is the moment a female driver reaches speeds of up to 130mph during a 13-mile police chase while high on a cocktail of powerful drugs.

Tia Paget, 34, raced past cars as she swerved between lanes shortly after taking cocaine and cannabis before eventually being halted by traffic and arrested.



Shocking footage shows the black Vauxhall Insignia dodging through traffic on a major road in Hampshire.

The car was seen cutting off a lorry on a roundabout during the chaotic and dangerous drive.



Paget initially failed to stop for police as her erratic driving triggered the chase back in April.

Swerving across lanes and dodging through cars, Paget put other road users in danger as she drove under the influence.



Despite reaching 130mph, cops managed to stay close to Paget until she ran herself into trouble in the form of an inescapable traffic jam.

Cops swiftly forced her out of the car and placed her in cuffs.



The crook then failed a cannabis and cocaine test at the roadside, along with small quantities of the drugs being found in her car.

Paget appeared at Portsmouth Crown Court on August 20 and was sentenced for charges of drug driving, dangerous driving, driving without insurance, possession of cocaine, and possession of cannabis.

She was banned from driving for four years, and handed a sentence of 10 months imprisonment which was suspended for two years.

Paget was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and 12 rehabilitation requirement days.

News.title: Cops probe death of man, 41, killed by falling sign at Christian festival
News.content:
THE death of a man killed by a falling sign at a Christian festival is being investigated by police.

They are examining whether or not the structure was properly secured before it collapsed, with witnesses claiming it was blown over by strong winds.



The 41-year-old man, from Eastbourne, East Sussex, was crushed when a huge wooden archway gave way on Friday.

Another six people were injured, two seriously.



Fred Abbott, a father of four, was sitting nearby when the structure fell at the sell-out Big Church Festival near Steyning, West Sussex.

He described hearing a “massive crack and bang” and joined an estimated 30 to 50 people who scrambled to lift the heavy wooden sign off the injured festival-goers.



Archbishop of Canterbury Dame Sarah Mullally was said to be “sad and shocked” by the fatality.

She said: “I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve.

“I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them.

“And I pray too for the other festival-goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.



“May the God of comfort and healing be with them all.”

The three-day event, founded in 2009, is the UK’s biggest Christian music festival with all 40,000 tickets sold.

Organisers later cancelled the event and said: “Big Church Festival is about bringing people together. That community is grieving. We are heartbroken.”



Det Chief Supt Richard McDonagh, of Sussex Police, said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts go out to the man’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.

“I recognise the immense distress this will have caused people at the festival, and we are working with a number of partners as we seek to establish exactly what happened.

“We’re urging anyone with information to come forward.”

News.title: Cleverly quits shadow cabinet to run for London mayor
News.content:
Conservative MP Sir James Cleverly has said he is resigning from the shadow cabinet to run for London mayor.

"I am putting myself forward to be the Conservative candidate for mayor of London, because our capital needs more than an administrator," he wrote in the Times, external.

Sir James said he has told Tory leader Kemi Badenoch he is stepping down as shadow housing secretary, saying: "I must be free to speak about every aspect of London's future and concentrate fully on winning this race."

The capital is not set to vote on a new mayor until May 2028. Labour incumbent Sir Sadiq Khan is yet to confirm whether he will seek an unprecedented fourth term.

The Conservatives are yet to pick their candidate for the London mayoral race.

A source close to Badenoch said Cleverly "is a formidable politician and will out-campaign Khan".

Sir James, who was foreign secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, wrote that he intended to make London a city to be proud of again.

"We must rebuild its reputation and make it, once again, the best place in the world to live, work, invest and build a business," he added.

A senior Conservative politician, Sir James has held a number of ministerial positions under three prime ministers - including roles as home secretary and education secretary.

The army reservist represented the Tories on the London Assembly before his election as MP for Braintree in 2015.

After rising through the backbenches, he unsuccessfully ran for Conservative party leader in 2024, losing out to Badenoch.

Reacting to Sir James's announcement, a source said Badenoch "really didn't want James to leave shadow cabinet", but believed "he will be a big asset in London".

Current London Mayor Sir Sadiq began his first term in 2016. Cleverly wrote that the capital has been "let down by Labour".

He accused Prime Minister Andy Burnham of treating London as a "cash cow: somewhere to tax, regulate, raid and blame".

Sir James said: "Londoners need homes they can afford to buy or rent. Entrepreneurs need to be able to start and grow businesses without being strangled by cost and regulation."

The last time Londoners voted for their mayor in May 2024, Sir Sadiq beat Conservative rival Susan Hall by more than 275,000 votes - representing a swing of 3.2% to Labour.

The mayor won nine of the 14 constituencies including two gains from the Tories, and gained 43.8% of the vote share.

Reform UK revealed its candidate for the May 2028 election in January when it announced Westminster City councillor Laila Cunningham would be standing.

Reacting on social media, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote the Conservatives are "done for", and said Cleverly "will not be the first Tory MP to give up any hope of winning their seat in Essex".

Cleverly has not resigned as an MP yet.

His announcement follows speculation in recent weeks that he would step down and launch a bid to become London's next mayor.

During his time at the London Assembly, Cleverly chaired the London Fire and Emergency Planning Authority, and also worked for Boris Johnson while he was mayor of London.

News.title: Rescue to continue overnight for 'in distress' vessel carrying five in the Channel
News.content:
Rescue efforts for a vessel "in distress" in the English Channel with five people on board will continue overnight, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency has said.

A helicopter, plane and lifeboats were launched on Saturday evening south-west of Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth.

Further details about the type of boat involved and the nature of the emergency have not been confirmed by officials.

RNLI lifeboats from Falmouth and Plymouth have been joined by a number of civilian vessels which are assisting the operation.

Several boats, primarily French fishing vessels, appear to be assisting rescue efforts, according to information from the maritime monitoring website Marine Traffic.

Around a dozen boats were clustered in an area off the coast of Plymouth in the early hours of Sunday.

A HM Coastguard aircraft has been flying over the same area, according to Flight Radar.

Moderate to rough conditions were expected off the coast of Plymouth overnight, the Met Office said.

Some thundery showers have been forecast, while visibility was expected to deteriorate at times.

News.title: I've been to Gamescom six times - here's what excited me this year
News.content:
Gamescom is the largest in-person gaming event in the world, and this year it lived up to expectations with big games on show from The Witcher 3's new expansion, to Alien: Isolation 2.

Last year over 350,000 people flocked to the halls of the Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany to get a chance to see and play the most hotly anticipated games.

This year that number of attendees is expected to have been even bigger, with the likes of Xbox and Sega showcasing games to the public alongside indie studios with only one or two developers.

This was my sixth time attending Gamescom, which never fails to make me excited about the games industry. Here are a few of the big things I got to check out this week.

News.title: British heavyweight Moses Itauma stretchered out after shock defeat in gruelling world title fight
News.content:
Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.

Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.

Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.

Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said.

"From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."

With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.

Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.

News.title: 97-year-old woman rescued after Nepali floods looked like 'a warrior'
News.content:
A 97-year-old woman pulled from flood debris in Nepal is recovering in hospital, according to her doctors.

Guna Maya Bohara's great-nephew, Dipak Bohara, has told BBC Nepali she looked like "a warrior" who had returned victorious from battle.

The operation to pull Bohara out of the rubble of her care home took four hours.

Bohara travelled from Kathmandu to help rescue his great-aunt.

Hundreds of people have been confirmed dead after Wednesday's flash floods, which scientists believe were triggered by a glacier collapsing in the Himalayan border region with Tibet.

Video produced by Mansi Kapur and Kamal Pariyar. Video edited by Suneth Perera, Jasmin Dyer and Andrew Webb.

More on this story here.

News.title: Satellite images reveal scale of flood devastation in Nepal villages
News.content:
New satellite imagery has revealed the scale of the devastation along Nepal's Trishuli River caused by Wednesday's deadly flash flood, triggered by a glacier collapse.

Before-and-after images show how sections of the valley, where a torrent of floodwater and debris surged through, destroyed villages, bridges and hydroelectric power stations.

Hundreds of people have been killed and thousands more are missing, Nepalese officials say.

Among the worst-hit locations reviewed by BBC Verify was a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing, which was engulfed by a rush of floodwater and captured on camera.

The satellite imagery from US-based intelligence firm Vantor, shows the site has been almost entirely washed away. Shocking CCTV footage showed the moment as the deluge of water swept over buildings as people tried to escape.

News.title: What we know about the 33 British nationals missing in Nepal
News.content:
Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country.

The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister.

"Please help us find her", Naresh Goyal told the BBC as he struggled to hold back his emotions.

On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding, search efforts have continued.

To help, the UK is deploying a rapid deployment team to Nepal to support British nationals affected in the region.

The specially-trained crisis response team is expected to arrive in Kathmandu on Saturday, a move that follows Prime Minister Andy Burnham's pledge of Â£5m worth of humanitarian support for relief and recovery efforts.

And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging.

News.title: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sister
News.content:
For years, Arthur Kermalvezen, the child of a sperm donor, saw possible fathers everywhere he went. "I imagined it might be my teacher, the people I saw on the bus... and I was very angry because it's impossible to live like this."

When, as an adult, he fell in love with Audrey, another sperm donor baby from Paris, the question became even more pressing.

Audrey describes the moment they met at a gathering for donor conceived activists in 2010 as "love at first sight" - but was this connection a romantic or genetic attraction?

When they were born, there were only two sperm banks in Paris and many men had made multiple donations - so there was a real possibility they could be half-siblings.

Before building a life together, Arthur and Audrey needed to know whether they were related. But in France, laws governing genetic testing and donor anonymity made finding the answer extremely difficult.

News.title: Christian festival 'devastated' after man's death
News.content:
Organisers of a Christian festival say they are "devastated" after a man died and six other people were injured by a falling sign.

Sussex Police said it had been called to the Big Church Festival at Wiston Park, near Steyning in West Sussex, at about 15:38 BST on Friday.

It was later confirmed a 41-year-old man from Eastbourne in East Sussex had died.

The Archbishop of Canterbury said she was "sad and shocked" to hear about the fatal incident.

Dame Sarah Mullally said: "I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve. I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them.

"And I pray too for the other festival goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.

"May the God of comfort and healing be with them all."

South East Coast Ambulance service said four of the six people injured were taken to local hospitals for further treatment, with two people having serious injuries.

The Big Church Festival, which describes itself as the UK's biggest Christian festival, was founded in 2009.

The festival began on Friday and was due to continue until Sunday, but a decision was made by organisers to cancel the remainder of the event after the incident.

"We are working with the emergency services, police and the Health and Safety Executive as they establish the circumstances surrounding today's incident," the organisers said.

"We are incredibly grateful to everyone who responded, and to our teams and community for the care they have shown one another."

News.title: Sarah Ferguson expected back in the UK 'shortly', source says
News.content:
Ferguson is expected to move into the six-bedroom home "imminently", which could be as soon as next week, the Sun reported, external.

It is believed she has been spending her time out of the public eye at an Alpine chalet in Verbier, Switzerland, since leaving Royal Lodge. Her belongings were collected from Mountbatten-Windsor's home in Sandringham this week, the newspaper added.

She had been keeping a low profile since losing her titles alongside Mountbatten-Windsor after she became mired in the scandal about her connections to Epstein, and faced calls to speak to US authorities after last year's release of millions of documents shed new light on their relationship.

In one email exchange from 2011, she appeared to privately apologise for her public rejection of Epstein, saying: "You have always been a steadfast, generous and supreme friend to me and my family."

A spokesperson for the duchess previously said the email was sent after Epstein had threatened to sue her for defamation - in an effort to convince him not to.

Another email suggested Ferguson took her daughters to see Epstein in the US days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes.

The emails do not indicate any wrongdoing.

Epstein was also ultimately the downfall of Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his titles by the King because of "serious lapses of judgment" over his friendship with the late paedophile. Mountbatten-Windsor has always denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.

Ferguson lost her courtesy royal divorcee title and reverted to her maiden name, and also lost the freedom of the city of York after councillors voted unanimously to remove the honour over the scandal.

Her expected return comes just days after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex came back to Britain with their children to begin a new life after six years living in the US.

News.title: Football fans pay tribute to crash death officers
News.content:
Football fans and players have paid tribute to two Cleveland Police officers who were killed in a crash on Teesside.

PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

There was a minute's applause in their memory ahead of Middlesbrough and West Bromwich Albion's Championship match at Riverside Stadium, as pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Matthew Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Seaton Carew FC coach Marcus Newing, who was friends with him, said the past week had been "horrendous", but seeing the "outpouring" from the nation had been "comforting".

"People would probably say that he's the goal of a dad and a husband," Newing said.

News.title: Strong winds and thunderstorms kick off the bank holiday weekend
News.content:
After weeks of scorching heat and drought the summer's swan song is set to be one of frequent downpours as well as gales for some.

Areas of heavy rain and showers are expected to sweep across parts of the UK on each day of the weekend, which is a bank holiday for many.

This could make for some soggy moments at many of the festivals taking place over the coming days.

Strong winds and gales may also cause problems for travellers and holidaymakers in southern parts of the UK.

News.title: Royal Navy warships track Russian vessels for three days in UK waters
News.content:
Royal Navy warships and a helicopter spent three days tracking Russian Navy vessels and sanctioned cargo ships in an "intense" operation in the North Sea and English Channel.

HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn used radars to monitor four vessels last week, while a Merlin helicopter provided surveillance from the sky.

"Since that successful operation, we have seen Russian shadow fleet vessels increasingly forced to change their routes, imposing significant cost and delays to their journeys," Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord and Chief of Naval Staff, said.

It comes as data shows Royal Navy activity to monitor Russian movements is up 25% so far this year compared to 2025.

During the August operation, the Royal Navy warships including a Type 45 destroyer and a Type 23 frigate, tracked Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko as it escorted sanctioned cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta south through the North Sea and into the English Channel.

The Royal Navy said Russia was "forced" to respond with "costly military resources" including the frigate Neustrashimy.

A statement said a Nato ally then took over monitoring off the coast of France, without specifying the country.

The operation comes after Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in June.

Marines joined by National Crime Agency (NCA) officers, with the support of the RAF, intercepted and boarded the Smyrtos in a six-hour operation - the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

NCA officers arrested an Indian national, 38, on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations and he was taken into custody.

News.title: Mother backs calls to stop killers' early release
News.content:
More than 30 families have called on the government to stop killers convicted of any form of manslaughter being released early to ease prison overcrowding in England and Wales.

In a letter to Justice Secretary Alex Norris, the families said they felt victims were "being asked to bear the consequences of the prison capacity crisis".

Signatories include Emma Webber, whose son Barnaby was stabbed to death in the Nottingham attacks in 2023, and whose killer Valdo Calocane was convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility.

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, Bridget Phillipson, Minister for Women and Equalities, defended the early release scheme.

She said the government had faced "some really difficult and unpalatable choices" in dealing with prison overcrowding and that they had faced "the wholesale collapse of the criminal justice system".

The scheme, external aims to ease prison overcrowding in England and Wales.

The families of those affected by homicide have called for those convicted of any form of manslaughter to be excluded.

Those convicted of murder and those serving sentences for rape, serious child sexual abuse and grooming offences are already excluded from the early release scheme.

News.title: Murder investigation after man found dead and child seriously injured
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a man was found dead alongside a seriously injured child in County Tyrone on Saturday morning.

A male has been arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder and remains in custody.

The incident took place in Lisnahull Road in Dungannon.

The child was taken to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children.

Police are currently at the scene and have said the public should avoid the area while enquiries continue.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said they received a 999 call at 11:08 BST on Saturday, following reports of an incident.

They dispatched a helicopter crew, three emergency crews, one advanced care paramedic, two ambulance officers and one HART (Hazardous Area Response Team) crew to the scene.

News.title: Woman detained in Egypt over 'sister's activism'
News.content:
A mother-of-four from Birmingham has been detained by the Egyptian authorities, with her husband and lawyer claiming it is due to her sister's online activism.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, from Handsworth Wood, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo in the early hours of Monday 17 August. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said this was 24 hours after Egyptian security forces "ram-raided" the property and told her: "You need to tell your sister to stop".

Three of el-Shazly's other siblings have also been detained, with her two brothers already being held when she was taken, and one of her sisters detained soon after.

The BBC has contacted the Egyptian consulate in London but has not had a response.

Moustapha said: "The family's a bit traumatised. [The children] are heartbroken.

"We really need the UK government to get their fingers out as quickly as possible."

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) said: "We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities."

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has accused “fear-mongering” politicians and journalists of hyping up “so-called measles deaths” as he defended the Trump administration in the face of a historic spike in U.S. measles cases.

"In 10 years, there have been three measles deaths in America,” Kennedy said during Saturday’s town hall even on Fox News, after being asked if the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine should be mandatory, given two recent measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania.

“There are now about 1.2 million deaths every year from food-induced illness. The media and certain demagogic politicians are constantly trying to scare us about infectious disease,” he said.

Kennedy referred to the deaths in Pennsylvania, announced by public health officials on Tuesday, as “so-called measles deaths” and alleged “the governor has not been able to point to any child who died from measles in Lancaster County.”

Public health officials quickly took issue with Kennedy’s comments, noting that the low prevalence of measles deaths was a direct result of widespread vaccination.

open image in gallery Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr tried to downplay the ongoing measles spike and accused Pennsylvania officials of potentially fabricating a pair of recent measles-related deaths during a Fox News town hall August 29 ( Reuters )

“Measles deaths are rare in America for one reason: MMR coverage has been near-universal for decades,” Dr. Jake Scott, a clinical professor of infectious diseases at Stanford University, wrote on X. “Before the vaccine, this country lost 400-500 people to measles every year, with 48,000 hospitalizations. He’s citing the vaccine’s own achievement as evidence we never needed it.

Throughout the week, Kennedy has been locked in a war of words with Pennsylvania officials over whether the state had seen a spate of new measles-related deaths.

On Tuesday, the state health department said it had “confirmed” two measles-related deaths among people who were unvaccinated against the disease, the state’s first such deaths in 35 years.

Later that day, Governor Josh Shapiro said at a press conference he had pressed Kennedy in a phone call over his long history of vaccine skepticism, which included a 2021 visit to Lancaster County where he reportedly made light of his own childhood case of measles.

“I was very, very blunt with him,” Shapiro, seen as a 2028 Democratic presidential contender, said.

“[I] made very clear that his actions and the rhetoric that’s coming from this administration are having a negative impact on communities across America, particularly right here in Pennsylvania,” Shapiro said.

Kennedy responded, claiming on social media that Shapiro’s administration may have “fabricated” the cases for political gain, though the state said it reported the cases to the CDC on Tuesday.

open image in gallery Pennsylvania health officials announced two measles-related deaths this week, the state’s first in 35 years ( Centers for Disease Control and Prevention )

Lancaster County Commissioner Josh Parsons has accused state officials of withholding information from the public and potentially announcing the cases prematurely.

Under the Trump administration, measles cases have surged to their highest level since 1991, and three unvaccinated people died from measles last year, the first reported measles deaths in the U.S. since 2015.

During his town hall, Kennedy insisted the MMR vaccine was safe and blamed the outbreak on declining vaccination rates during the COVID-19 pandemic, a time when “a lot of people across the globe lost faith in the public health system.”

Prior to his time in office, Kennedy was a prominent anti-vaccine activist, and he has made various misleading and false statements about the MMR vaccine since being appointed, including that vaccines aren’t “safety tested” and that immunity from the vaccine wanes quickly.

President Donald Trump on Saturday posted an apparently AI-generated video depicting an army of buff, bequiffed and heavily-armed “Donald Ducks” patrolling the shores of “Lake America.”

Hours later, while he was at his Virginia golf course, the president posted another AI-generated video, this time showing himself knocking over a “Welcome to Lake Ontario” sign and installing a “Welcome to Lake America” one in its place. He then dances to the Village People’s “YMCA.”

The posts followed Trump’s executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” amid a bitter tariff war with Canada, a longtime U.S. ally and trading partner.

Set to the theme song from Hawaii Five-O, a 34-second clip shows a squadron of Canada geese marching near the Great Lake. The birds have human arms, carry assault rifles and sport the president’s signature blond pouf of hair.

The geese then fire their weapons into the air as fireworks erupt over the skyline of a nearby city — which appears to resemble Toronto.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump posted an apparently AI-generated video of 'Lake America' being patrolled by an army of buff and bequiffed 'Donald Ducks' ( @RealDonaldTrump, Truth Social )

Earlier this week, Trump announced that the U.S. was giving “serious consideration” to rebranding Lake Ontario, which straddles the U.S.-Canada border. He also posted a TikTok video showing himself using a Sharpie to mark up a map of the lake.

“We’re gonna make a little change; we’re gonna call it something different than Lake Ontario,” the 80-year-old president said in the clip.

open image in gallery Trump posted another AI-generated video that shows the president knocking over a sign for Lake Ontario then dancing to the Village People ( @RealDonaldTrump, Truth Social )

Any doubt that the effort was simply trolling evaporated Thursday, when Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to refer to Lake Ontario as “Lake America” in all official documents and records. The move echoed his similar effort last year to rebrand the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.”

Although the president can direct how the federal government refers to geographic features, he cannot compel foreign nations, private entities or even U.S. states to follow his lead.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney responded to the missive in a Thursday post on X.

“The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means ‘the lake is beautiful, the lake is big,’” he wrote. “The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America.”

“We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms,” he added. “Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario – then, now and always.”

open image in gallery Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to refer to Lake Ontario as ‘Lake America’ in all official documents and records ( Getty Images )

Relations between the U.S. and Canada have deteriorated since Trump took office, including as a result of his repeated suggestion that Canada should become the “51st state.” Tensions escalated further this week over trade.

On August 22, the U.S. imposed 50 percent tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian exports after last-minute talks between Ottawa and Washington broke down. The Trump administration has accused Canada of discriminating against U.S. businesses.

Carney, who has denied Trump’s accusations, likened the levies to an act of war. He retaliated with tariffs of up to 50 percent on a range of U.S. goods.

The trade war has also spilled into a war of words. This week, Trump singled out Ontario Premier Doug Ford in a Truth Social post, describing him as a blustering “flunky” who needs to “fall in line.”

At a news conference, Ford responded by calling Trump a “dictator,” a “bully” and the “king of bankruptcies.” He also told Trump to “kiss my a**.”

The remains of 19 dead migrants, including children, were found in the Arizona desert near the U.S.-Mexico border last month, a two-year record, according to data from the Pima County Office of the Medical Examiner and the advocacy group Humane Borders.

Among the deceased, five appeared to have been dead for less than a day and two had been dead for less than a week when they were found.

“This is a persistent and perennial problem, it's not just a July 2026 problem,” Brad Jones, a political science professor at the UC Davis Global Migration Center and a Humane Borders board member, told the Arizona Daily Star.

“It does ebb and flow, but it never goes away,” he said. “We’ve never had a period of zero recovered remains” since Humane Borders was founded in 2000, acording to Jones.

The record number of deaths, likely an undercount, is all the more striking because border crossings have plunged overall since Donald Trump took office and tightened a variety of immigration policies, including effectively cutting off all asylum claims and restricting entries at the southern border.

There were nearly 10 times fewer encounters between Border Patrol agents and migrants in July 2026 than during the same month in 2024, the final full year of Joe Biden’s administration.

open image in gallery The remains of 19 dead migrants, including children, were found in the Arizona desert near the U.S.-Mexico border in July 2026, a two-year record ( AP )

As The Independent has reported, the U.S. has long pursued a strategy of “prevention through deference,” using military-style security infrastructure such as walls and barbed wire at popular points of entry to push migrants into remote rural areas spanning the lengthy U.S.-Mexico border, in the hopes that the danger of the crossing will prevent future migration.

Critics argue that undocumented immigration into the U.S. is often driven by life-or-death factors and migrants will make the journey regardless of what kind of barriers are in their way, exposing already-vulnerable people to injury and death along the mountains, rivers and deserts of the borderlands.

The Trump administration has continued to fortify the border, thanks in part to a $46 billion infusion of funds from Congress to continue building its signature border wall, which was largely paused during the Biden administration.

Border construction efforts have continued across Arizona, New Mexico and Texas, despite opposition from indigenous tribes, environmental advocates and park boosters, who have been particularly incensed by a plan to add new border security infrastructure within Big Bend National Park, an area that’s not a high-traffic illegal immigration zone.

open image in gallery The Trump administration has continued building out its signature border wall, thanks to a $46 billion infusion of funds from Congress, despite widespread opposition in border communities across the Southwest ( Getty )

In addition to adding new physical barriers at the border, the Trump administration has sought massive changes to the legal regime along the frontier.

The White House has argued migration into the U.S. constitutes an invasion and gives the administration the power to remove undocumented border crossers without giving them a chance to seek asylum, a right which is protected under U.S. and human rights law. Lower courts have blocked the policy, though the Trump administration is seeking a Supreme Court appeal.

The administration has also revoked temporary protected status rights for people from a variety of nations, policies which had given tens of thousands of immigrants from unstable regions reprieve from deportation.

Last year, 32 people died in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody, the most deaths in more than two decades.

Moses Itauma was taken to hospital as a precautionary measure after his IBF world heavyweight title bid ended in a ninth-round stoppage by new champion Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma was carried from the ring on a stretcher following an explosive clash for the vacant belt at The O2 that saw Hrgovic become Croatia’s first champion in the division.

The 21-year-old from Kent was in complete command of the fight but had punched himself out in search of the knockout and was exhausted when referee Howard Foster came to his rescue with trainer Ben Davison also throwing in the towel.

“Moses has gone to the hospital for a check up,” promoter Frank Warren said.

“It’s precautionary that he’s gone to the hospital. That’s what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer’s health.

open image in gallery Hrgovic and Itauma slugged it out in the final rounds (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

“He’s there and he’s in the best place. We’ll see what happens when I’ve got a report. We’ll obviously let everybody know.

“He’s done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high paced, fast fight for both the guys. It was just edge of your seat stuff all the way through.”

Itauma reined down blows on Hrgovic for the first seven rounds but the wily 34-year-old was able to soak up the punishment and then took control in the eighth and ninth rounds.

Showing a granite chin and enormous heart, he won the exchanges as the rivals went toe to toe and Itauma lurched across the ring until Foster intervened.

The clash had been billed ‘Witness History’ in anticipation of Itauma being crowned Britain’s youngest ever world heavyweight champion, but his career has stalled and Warren was unable to guarantee he would be back.

“I don’t know what he’s going to say,” Warren said. “I’m sure he’s a fighting man. He showed that right to the end. At the end, that’s the type of fight it was – they were standing there just letting bombs go.

open image in gallery Itauma started well but tired (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

“I don’t even know how he feels mentally. Mentally, he’s going to be completely down. We’re going to have to talk to him and lift him and see what he’s like.

“It’s going to take some time. He’s going to have a nice break. It’s not even the time to talk about it with him at the moment.

“It’s something we’re probably doing in two weeks or even a month’s time, see where we go with it.”

Hrgovic must now take on the IBF’s mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez, who was paid step aside money to enable him to face Itauma.

“I can’t believe it’s happening,” he said. My head is ringing from everything. It will take time for my feelings to settle. But I can’t believe that after 20 years I have my dream.

“God gave me the best possible gift to fight to win a world title against the best guy in the division. The most talented guy in the division. There is no better way for me to become a world champion.”

News.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic LIVE: Result and reaction as Briton’s towel comes in before he leaves on stretcher
News.content:
Moses Itauma slapped by Filip Hrgovic at weigh-in ahead of heavyweight showdown

Moses Itauma suffered the first loss of his career on Saturday, as he was stunned by Filip Hrgovic in a world heavyweight title thriller.

Itauma, 21, was aiming to become the second-youngest heavyweight champion ever – only after Mike Tyson – but his corner threw in the towel in round nine to end that dream.

London’s O2 Arena crowd was left in shock as Hrgovic became Croatia’s first-ever world heavyweight champion, having survived his British foe’s best shots before turning the tide to collect the vacant IBF belt.

Hrgovic, 34, demonstrated an incredible chin, and Itauma tired as the fight wore on, with his technique deserting him and his legs growing wobbly. And Hrgovic capitalised by pouring on punches, leading Itauma’s coach Ben Davison to throw in the towel.

A village cricket player has raised enough money to fly by helicopter from his wedding in Wales to Lord’s Cricket Ground to captain his team in a national final.

Peter Melhuish is due to marry his fiancée Izzy Upton in North Wales next Saturday - which meant he looked set to miss out on playing for his team, Blackheath Cricket Club in Guildford, in the final of the Cawston Press Village Cup at Lord’s.

But in a bid to overcome the dilemma, the club – who Mr Melhuish has played for since he was aged six – set up a fundraiser to have him flown by helicopter from his wedding venue in Wales to the stadium in northwest London.

The club has now raised over £6,000, well over the £4,500 goal for the ride, with a £1,000 donation from Piers Morgan helping him hit the target.

open image in gallery Peter Melhuish, 32, with his wife-to-be Izzy Upton, also 32, who will get married on Saturday ( Blackheath Cricket Club )

“For many a young cricketer there are two great dreams in his life, the one where he marries the beautiful girl in the idyllic hills of North Wales, and the one where he plays cricket for his boyhood team at Lord’s,” said Blackheath Cricket Club in a statement for the fundraiser.

“Very few people are lucky enough ever to achieve both of those dreams, but vanishingly few are UN-lucky enough to have them both happen within 24 hours of each other!”

After the fundraising target was met, the club said: “We've done it! Pete and Izzy will be able to fly from their wedding in North Wales on 5th September to Lord's Cricket Ground by 10am on 6th September, to fulfil Pete's lifetime ambition of playing for Blackheath Cricket Club in the final of the National Village Cup.”

The only other option would have been for Mr Melhuish to take a taxi at 5am to reach the game at 10:30am. Flying by helicopter means he will be able to make the trip in around 90 minutes.

Mr Melhuish explained that his partner had been very understanding about the situation.

"We've been organising the wedding for well over a year so the fixtures for the Village Cup hadn't even come out when we started organising it,” he told the BBC.

"She's been really supportive and very understanding of how much it means, not just to me but the club too.”

Any surplus funds will be donated to Kids for Kids, a UK-based charity that has been helping children in Darfur, Ethiopia since 2011.

“It's a cause that was dear to the heart of Pete's Mum and he's raising the money in memory of her,” read a statement by Blackheath.

Russian strikes have killed at least 37 people in Kyiv, most of them from a care home for the elderly, according to local Ukrainian officials.

It marks the deadliest attack on Ukraine’s capital this year, the Associated Press reports.

The strikes hit an ammunition depot, sparking a fire in the Bucha district overnight that spread to surrounding areas.

Dozens were injured with nearby infrastructure including residential buildings and the care facility for the elderly and people with disabilities suffering “significant damage”.

Volodymyr Zelensky has vowed to punish those responsible and said criminal cases had already been opened on charges of official negligence.

He described it as a “terrible situation and terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people”.

Meanwhile, Russia’s defence ministry said it had successfully tested a nuclear-capable intercontinental ballistic missile that could reach the US.

The missile, which has a range of more than 6,700km, was fired from the Arkhangelsk region and reached its designated target at the Kura test site in Kamchatka.

It comes just days after CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow to warn Russia off any attack on a Nato attack according to reports. The Kremlin denied the claims and accused western media of “scare-stories”.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
The 34-year-old Hrgovic had gone into the fight as the underdog, with Itauma heavily fancied after a precocious early career. Had the Briton won, he would have maintained his undefeated record and become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing.

Itauma, 21, is famous for his early stoppages. He had never previously gone past six rounds in the ring, and he raced out of his corner for the first two rounds in pursuit of victory.

The youngster dominated the early exchanges and forced a standing count for Hrgovic as his opponent stumbled after a heavy blow, with the referee intervening. At that point it looked as if he would become just another of Itauma’s victims.

However, the older man proved the value of his chin as he took plenty of jabs and hooks to the face, but only rarely looked rattled. Occasionally, he sent some of his own jabs back in Itauma’s direction, but for most of the fight he looked to be holding on, just in case something happened to rescue him.

Salvation eventually came, as it became suddenly clear that Itauma simply was not conditioned for a fight that would go the distance. In round eight, the two traded blows and looked totally spent.

They both took their minute to rest, but it was Hrgovic who sucked the most oxygen into his lungs. The Croatian punished Itauma from the opening seconds and it became evident that the Briton did not have the energy to remain upright and competently defend himself. While he bravely attempted a few more wild swings, he bounced off the ropes worryingly and the referee stepped in to bring the fight to a close.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

News.title: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow
News.content:
Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

News.title: England light years ahead of lamentable Pakistan
News.content:
Who needs Ben Stokes? Actually, it is hard to think of any side that would need him against this Pakistan team.

After just five days of cricket, and despite their own limitations with the bat, England are on the cusp of a series victory at Lord’s with a 261-run lead and power to add thanks to the prowess of a seam attack that has emerged quickly from the shadow of its former captain.

It will take longer to feel the full effects of Stokes’s absence. When England need a spinner in the side, they will miss the seam-bowling all-rounder to balance the XI. There will be times when they are up against it on a flat deck on a boiling day and be desperate for Stokes’s sheer will to win. It is still hard to think he will not play some part in the Ashes next summer.

For the final two years of his career it was Stokes’s bowling that was top class, his batting having become ordinary. But with bowlers of the quality of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson gelling, England are more than making up for Stokes’s retirement. This bowling attack against Pakistan’s batting was a complete mismatch.

Joe Root has stepped into Stokes’s shoes confidently, laying down the law off the field and tactically he has been spot on, although Pakistan have hardly stretched him. The only stir they have made since arriving was the stink they kicked up over Sky Sports’ interview with Imran Khan’s sons.

Conclusions are impossible to draw with any confidence against such poor opponents. Sri Lanka and West Indies two years ago put up a stronger fight in the first two Tests of their series. Tamim Iqbal scored two hundreds as Bangladesh at least landed some blows in 2010. Pakistan have managed one fifty in three innings and were bowled out for 171 and 135 at Headingley and a lamentable 110 here.

They were a batsman down at Lord’s because of a calf injury to opener Imam-ul-Haq, but only reached three figures because England dropped top scorer Azan Awais on eight; he went on to score 46.

England’s batting is hardly firing, but with a 180 first-innings lead, they could afford to be 13 for two without panic spreading. Losing Root for 24 kept Pakistan interested, but Emilio Gay toughed it out in the gloom to reach stumps unbeaten on 30; England 81 for three, light years ahead in the game.

Robinson’s astonishing figures of 13-6-11-4 set him on the way for a probable third man-of-the-match award in a row and continued his unexpected resurgence. Rarely did his pace go above 78mph, he just landed the ball time and again on a length and let movement off the seam do the rest.

News.title: I’ve lived in Norfolk for more than 30 years. Here’s how to explore England’s windswept east
News.content:
Norfolk’s vast sandy beaches are its chief draw for visitors: even on the busiest summer day there is always space for games, kite-flying or a family picnic in the dunes. Boating, crabbing, digging for cockles and wading in creeks provides hours of entertainment for all.

But there’s much more to Norfolk’s coast than its beaches. It’s also a landscape of dense pine forest and large expanses of salt marsh, which flush purple with sea-lavender in August. Birdlife is astonishingly rich, and wildflowers include yellow-horned poppies and lilac-flowering sea pea.

Inland, the undulating countryside and sleepy flint-built villages are perfect for gentle cycling, walking or touring by car. Grand stately homes make enjoyable days out, and almost every village has a sublimely beautiful medieval church at its centre.

Lively Georgian towns such as Burnham Market and Holt offer quirky shopping – and, wherever you are, you’re never far from an atmospheric pamment-floored pub serving local ales, or an excellent delicatessen selling the region’s specialities. Look out for pungent cheeses, smoked fish and salt-marsh flavoured honey.

Sports.title: Forget Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, Ezri Konsa is the man to finally help Arsenal win the Champions League, says icon
Sports.content:
BACARY SAGNA has tipped Ezri Konsa to be the missing piece that wins Arsenal the Champions League.

Defender Konsa joined the Gunners in a £51million move from Aston Villa last week — and could make his debut against his former side at Villa Park on Monday.



The England man’s arrival at Arsenal may not be the most glamorous transfer, particularly after the club spent the summer pining after superstars such as Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers.

But the move was necessary for manager Mikel Arteta, who is expected to be without centre-back William Saliba for a lengthy portion of the season due to a back injury.



Konsa, 28, has been brought in to fill the gap left in Saliba’s absence and to offer high-quality competition when the Frenchman returns.

And former Arsenal right-back Sagna — who made 284 appearances for the Gunners up until 2014 — is convinced the rivalry Konsa will offer could be vital in the club’s quest to finally taste European success.

Speaking to SunSport via prediction markets reviewer Action Network, Sagna, 43, said: “To be competitive, you need to have two players in each position and the season is long.

“It’s not, of course, a competition inside the squad. The squad is genuine because all the players get on well together.

“But to be competitive and successful, players need to understand that they need a back-up.

“So whoever plays doesn’t lower the level of the team — and I think if Arsenal want to go for higher competitions and reach the dream, which is probably to win the Champions League, Konsa is the type of player you need to have.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“You need players with different profiles. Positions need to be covered and Mikel Arteta understands this.”

Arteta has already splashed out on bringing Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge and Newcastle’s Bruno Guimaraes to North London this summer — and still hopes to bolster his attack before Tuesday’s deadline.

But it could be Konsa who proves to be Arsenal’s most vital signing.

The Gunners relied heavily on their defence to finally lift the Premier League title after a 22-year wait last season and may have to do so again this term.

Arteta has built his foundations on a solid back line.



That was evidenced by the fact that Saliba, Gabriel, Jurrien Timber and David Raya were all named in the PFA Team of the Year this week.

Despite their success, Konsa bettered all of Arsenal’s defenders last season regarding ground-duel and tackle success rates. He was also a key man in England’s World Cup squad this summer.

Konsa’s combative style has made him one of the best defenders in the Premier League and it is a big reason why Sagna thinks he will be a success in N5.



The Frenchman, who also played for Manchester City, added: “He has established himself with Aston Villa and with England.

“I think he had a good tournament and he’s so good one-on-one. He’s not scared to be one-on-one.

“He is good in challenges and duels — and this is what Arsenal need because most of the time, having possession of the ball exposes you — and you need this type of player who has the brain to defend in one-on-one situations. He’s one of them.

“Having the ball and having so much possession is one thing but being able to defend one-on-one like Saliba has been doing, like Gabriel has been doing, like Konsa is able to do, I think it’s important for the squad.”

Sports.title: Cody Gakpo picks Man City as talks over £85m transfer accelerate despite Tottenham interest as Barcola closes in on Reds
Sports.content:

And he now has his man in £123m Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain who is due on Merseyside this weekend for a medical.

Gakpo featured in Liverpool’s 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest on Saturday afternoon.

He also scored in Liverpool’s first match of the Premier League season, which also ended in a 2-2 draw but against Newcastle.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi confirms THREE stars demanded to quit Tottenham as he explains Richarlison absence from Newcastle loss
Sports.content:
SPURS boss Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that THREE players have asked to leave the club.

The Tottenham manager, after the 2-0 loss to Newcastle, admitted that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr are determined to force a move within the next few days.



Richarlison has one year left on his current deal and former club Everton are interested.

De Zerbi said: “He said too many times he wanted to leave. Danso came two days ago and said he wants to leave.



“Sarr is the same. He suffered a small injury but is almost ready to train.

“You can’t buy mentality. Football like a magic thing. You can change many players in one window and find the balance immediately or you need more time.



“I would like to do it quickly as soon as possible. The plan, the project of the club and what we are doing is to rebuild a new team with new players.”

Tottenham want around £20million for Sarr so he looks certain to leave before the transfer window shuts on Tuesday.

Spurs continued their difficult start to the season – despite splashing out £300m on new signings – as they suffered successive defeats without a goal.

The home side had a decent first half but Newcastle took their chances in the second as Anthony Elanga and Yoanne Wissa struck.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

De Zerbi insists Spurs “will not panic” despite their bad start and feels the team were “unlucky” in their defeat.

He said after the game: “Forget the result. I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result.

“We will not panic. I know very well where we are going, what the plan is and what difficult problems we could find in our way.

“I am sorry for the fans and sorry for the players for the result but we have to improve and to change two seasons like the last two is impossible in 10 days and with people in the transfer market.



“We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection with the players because last season before the end of the season we were in the Championship and we stayed up together.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll dodges prison in court cash row with ex-wife Billi Mucklow
Sports.content:
FORMER England footie ace Andy Carroll has dodged prison in a court cash row with his reality star ex-wife.

A judge said he could have been jailed after repeatedly breaching an order banning him from non-essential spending.



Chelmsford county court heard that Carroll spent £69,181 that should have been preserved ahead of a five-day financial hearing next month.

But his lawyer said: “I would submit £69,000 is a drop in the ocean, given how much is involved, including significant legal fees.”



In the 2019 Sunday Times Rich List, Carroll had a ­fortune of £19million.

The 37-year-old faced ­ex-Towie star Billi Mucklow, 38, as he admitted five breaches of a financial order.

He is said to have splashed out £5,556 for new wheels on his car, given £10,000 to his girlfriend’s brother and paid for his parents’ building work.

Jenna Lucas, for Ms Mucklow, insisted: “Nothing was necessary expenditure. He has, I submit, thumbed his nose at the order of this court.”

But Lauren Lanson, for Carroll, said: “He is not the most organised individual with control of his finances.

“He has other people who do that. He focuses on his work as a professional footballer.”



Carroll, who attended court with girlfriend Lou Teasdale, was hit with a fine of £20,000 after District Judge Teresa Foss reckoned that a prison term would be “too high a sanction”.

He faces trial next year over allegations that he broke a non-molestation order.

The ex-Newcastle, Liverpool and West Ham star joined National League South side Dagenham and Redbridge in 2025 after spells with French clubs Amiens and Bordeaux.

Sports.title: Prem assistant ref Simon Bennett suspended after married £110k a year official ‘behaved inappropriately with a woman’
Sports.content:
PREMIER League assistant referee Simon Bennett has been suspended over ­allegations of inappropriate behaviour with a woman.

The married £110,000-a-year senior linesman has not officiated this season after a probe was launched when concerns were raised about his conduct.



He last ran the line on May 24, the final day of last season, in Brighton’s 3-0 home defeat to Man United.

The former teacher, 41, had been selected and listed as an official by the Premier League for this season but has now gone to ground, it is said.



A source told The Sun on Sunday: “He has closed all his social media accounts and pretty much disappeared since he was suspended.

“The investigation is into his inappropriate behaviour with a woman.



“It has obviously raised eyebrows in the refereeing world because it goes against the grain of the job itself.

“Refs are supposed to ensure high standards on the pitch, so you’d hope they would do the same off the pitch.



“But we have to await the findings of the investigation now.”

Bennett, of Kidsgrove, Staffs, studied at Manchester Metropolitan University and taught at The Fallibroome ­Academy in Macclesfield, Cheshire, before becoming a full-time official.

He has worked in the Premier League since 2011 and it is not known if he is still being paid.

He has been on Fifa’s assistant referees list since 2013. He occasionally acts as an assistant video referee.

Refereeing body Professional Game Match Officials Limited, now called Pro Ref, the FA and Bennett have all declined to comment.

Sports.title: Everton fans threaten to RIOT if club sells teen sensation Harrison Armstrong as Nottingham Forest prepare £40m bid
Sports.content:
EVERTON fans are threatening they will RIOT if the club sells teenage sensation Harrison Armstrong.

Nottingham Forest are ready to pay £40million for the midfielder, 19, who played 87 minutes of the Toffees’ 1-1 draw at Bournemouth.



And travelling Everton fans let the board know their feelings about a potential late transfer.

They repeatedly chanted: “Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand… if you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands.”



But Everton boss David Moyes conceded he did not know whether Armstrong will be flogged.

When Moyes, 63, was asked if he will have the final say on Armstrong’s future and whether he expected him to stay on Merseyside, he replied: “Not sure yet.”

Armstrong has made 24 Everton appearances and was last season’s Young Player of the Season.

Forest boss Oliver Glasner is hopeful Everton can be persuaded to sell.
