Sports.title: ‘Blown away’ – Michael Owen can’t believe the reaction to new behind-the-scenes documentary about his life
Sports.content:
MICHAEL OWEN has admitted he is “blown away” by the reaction to his new documentary after it soared to No 2 in the Amazon Prime charts.

The former England striker’s new show Meet The Owens gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at his family life.



It features himself, wife Louise, daughters Gemma, Emily and Jessica and son James.

But some critics have panned the show, with the Independent calling it “boring” and “tedious”.



However, Owen has been pleased to see fans have been tuning in after pointing out its high ranking on Amazon.

He posted a picture of his show being placed at No 2 on X and wrote: “Absolutely blown away that Meet The Owens is at No2 after just 24 hours!



“The feedback has been incredible. Thanks for watching, I’m glad you’re all enjoying it!”

Fans replied by calling the show “a great watch” and “excellent insight into your family”.

One added: “It’s actually decent. Good insight into the world of horse racing too.”

Owen was hoping his new show would help get rid of his “most boring man title” and show a new side to him.

The documentary aims to put the Owens on the map and rival famous sporting families like the Beckhams, the Rooneys and the Furys.

It follows Owen at his huge, £4million North Wales mansion, and he also shows off his impressive work at racehorse training facility Manor House Stables, which he founded in 2006.

The show also showcases his daughter Gemma and her horse racing career.

She features heavily and will no doubt attract new fans after her stint on Love Island.



But some have taken issue with some of the more mundane elements of the show – including Owen eating dairylea cheese triangles on toast and his passion for orcas.

Owen was a superstar in his football days as he won the Ballon d’Or in 2001 while playing for Liverpool.

‌



"[It] would have happened, definitely. You stop [the game] because you want to sub [but] it doesn't happen.

“The quick throw-in, because we are waiting for the subs, so if I ask for the sub, and I already asked and I complained even the previous time that the ball went out and everyone was - even the supporters, I think they were shouting - aware of the situation, but I don't know the reason why they haven't done it. And the penalty, I leave you to decide if it's a penalty or not.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Ex-Premier League referee Graham Scott has now issued his thoughts on the incident and claimed that the technology is now outdated, albeit Iraola’s own complaints might have been exaggerated.

Taking to X, he wrote: “The subs boards are not fit for purpose. Each number has to be entered manually, and they only count up one at a time. Entering number 38 on its own could take several seconds and there are six numbers to plug in here.

“Also, the sponsors’ advertising makes them heavy and unwieldy, which is why the 4th has them on the ground. In UEFA comps the clubs have to enter the numbers themselves, which means they can get the subs done quicker. The PL only did this during Covid.

‌



View 2 Images Graham Scott has offered his take on the controversy surrounding Liverpool's draw with Nottingham Forest (Image: Getty Images)

“The 4th official would have had to check and double check the names and numbers of all six players involved in the substitutions against the official team sheet in case the club has made an error, which happens frequently enough to make such checks necessary.

After a fan suggested it took not take three minutes to make a substitution, he replied: “It shouldn’t take three minutes, agreed. But we have no evidence that it did, only Iraola’s word for it. I’ve stood next to him many times and say there’s just a chance he’s exaggerating for effect and to deflect from his goalkeeper’s rash challenge. I could be wrong, obvs.”

Sports.title: Liverpool star Cody Gakpo selects next club as talks on to complete late transfer
Sports.content:
Liverpool star Cody Gakpo selects next club as talks on to complete late transfer

Liverpool star Cody Gakpo has been linked with an exit before Tuesday’s transfer deadline and it appears that the Dutchman has now made a decision over where his future lies

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo was linked with both Man City and Tottenham (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool star Cody Gakpo has turned down a move to Tottenham in favour of Manchester City.

‌



The Dutchman, 27, has been linked with a move away from Anfield this summer, both City and Spurs having expressed an interest in him.

‌



The North London side remained keen on signing Gakpo despite having completed a double deal for Man City duo Savio and Omar Marmoush over the past week.

‌



But it appears that Gakpo is not keen on a switch to North London after all. Gakpo has decided to join Enzo Maresca’s side, with all parties now thought to be in talks to find an agreement.

Gakpo joined Liverpool in December 2022 in a deal worth a reported £37million. He has gone on to score 50 goals and 23 assists in 180 appearances in all competitions.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Gakpo only signed a new five-year deal with Liverpool last year, with that contract set to run until 2030. He provided an assist in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest, having started the game on the right flank.

Asked if the former PSV star could be an option in that position going forward, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said: “With the wingers, obviously normally they have a preferred position, but we normally analyse the match-ups, analyse what they have to do on one side, what they need to do on the other side.

“We decided with Rio [Ngumoha] and Victor [Munoz] to change them at the end. I think they have to get used [to that]. I think he [Gakpo] was going to be one of the subs when we scored the goal, he made a great play and then we were creating momentum.

‌



View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has a goal and an assist from the opening two games of the season (Image: Getty Images)

“I decided to leave them a little bit more - three, four minutes - to see if we could use this momentum to score a second one. When it went a little bit more plain, we decided to do those subs. That goal and the other one were, I think, very good goals.”

On any more potential incomings at Anfield before Tuesday’s deadline, the Spaniard added: “I cannot tell you anything different right now. It's true that there are things going on, like normal because we are talking about the last weeks of the market, but now we have to wait.

Article continues below

“I'm looking forward to having the squad [on] September 2, [so we can say] this is who we are and working with certainties. Now everything is quite like uncertain and it's the same for every team, but it's how the competition works. Now we have to wait just some [more] days and work with what we have after the market closes.”

Sports.title: Liverpool ‘don’t trust’ Alexander Isak as striker makes feelings clear on Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool ‘don’t trust’ Alexander Isak as striker makes feelings clear on Andoni Iraola

Liverpool star Alexander Isak scored his first goal of the season in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest after a slow debut campaign and Joe Hart believes there is still an ongoing issue

View 2 Images Isak struggled in his debut campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Joe Hart claims Alexander Isak still isn’t trusted at Liverpool despite having scored his first goal of the season. The Swedish striker completed a £125million move to Anfield from Newcastle last summer.

‌



His first season was hugely disrupted by injury and he went on to score just four times across his debut campaign. Isak is already off the mark, having netted in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest.

‌



But apart from that, he looked isolated in Andoni Iraola’s system. In analysing his performance, former Manchester City star Joe Hart has claimed that Isak hasn’t quite earned the trust of his teammates yet.

‌



Speaking to BBC Sport, he said: "It is clear that Liverpool haven't worked out how to play with Alexander Isak yet. At Newcastle everything flowed through him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“That was down to a trust thing that they had built up over time - their midfield knew exactly where he was and they didn't even need to look up as he'd be there waiting.

‌



"At Liverpool that trust just isn't there at the moment - no-one is feeling it and he isn't that central point, which is leading to him looking lost and isolated."

Hart added: "Andoni Iraola has some big decisions to make. Does he base his team round him [Isak] or does he try to find a different solution within his squad? In my opinion he's got to commit to what the club have done by investing so heavily in Isak.

View 2 Images Isak netted his first goal of the season against Forest (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"There's no point signing these players if you aren't going to use them properly and play to their strengths. There's no doubting Isak's quality - they are just at a bit of a crossroads at the moment."

While Hart believes that Isak still has some work to do, the striker himself has had his say on Liverpool’s stuttering start to the season and believes they will hit top form with time.

He said: “I think there's no problem in fighting spirit and never giving up. I think we showed that last week as well. Obviously we started the game pretty bad today as well. When we gained momentum by scoring a goal, that's where we need to be better, I think, because again today we conceded quite quickly after that. But from the position we were [in], it's always good to get something out of the game."

Article continues below

He added: “It's been good [working under Iraola]. There's always time to get used to a new playing style and a new manager. But we are really working hard to try to play the game he wants us to play and I think when we start doing that better, I have no doubt that the results will come.”

Sports.title: Arsenal complete Man Utd transfer raid as youngster explains Old Trafford exit
Sports.content:
Arsenal complete Man Utd transfer raid as youngster explains Old Trafford exit

Manchester United have raided Arsenal’s academy a number of times over the past couple of seasons but the Gunners have now got their own back with a swoop for James Scanlon

View 2 Images James Scanlon has left Manchester United for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United starlet James Scanlon has completed a move to Premier League rivals Arsenal - and could be joined by a former teammate. Scanlon, 19, was linked with a move to north London earlier this summer and has now seen his switch rubber-stamped.

‌



Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, the forward said: “It’s a pleasure to be here, I can’t wait to get started. I’ve been waiting to get this over the line, so I’m buzzing to be here.

‌



“My family are massive to me, so to have them here for this special day is only going to make it better.”

‌



He added: “You can see that everyone here is hungrier for more, hungrier to get better and I think that’s something I believe I can add to and want to be a part of as well.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I like to score goals, assist, so hopefully I can excite players who watch me. I’m looking forward to playing, representing the badge, improving and hopefully showing people what I can do.”

‌



Scanlon departs Old Trafford having progressed through the Red Devils academy. He became a regular for the under-21 side, before joining Swindon Town on loan and scored once in six appearances.

Scanlon’s move to Arsenal could be very quickly followed by another. Previous reports also suggested they were interested in a move for United's Habeeb Ogunneye, who was with Newport County last season.

Arsenal’s moves also see them continuing their push to sign promising young players. 16-year-old England youth international striker Vincent Joseph joined the club after leaving Liverpool, a tribunal now set to decide the fee that the Gunners will have to pay.

‌



View 2 Images Igor Tyjon has also signed for Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Mylo Bernard has joined the club from Crystal Palace, while Elijah Upson departed Tottenham to move across North London. Axel Donczew is also expected to be signed from Cardiff City following an impressive breakout year in Wales.

Igor Tyjon has also been recruited from Blackburn Rovers. He said: "It feels amazing. I've waited a long time for this and I can't wait to get started.

‌



“It's a dream come true for [my family] as well, it's always a nice feeling when you make your family happy, so I'm buzzing for them as well.

"Who doesn't want to join the champions? I can't wait to be part of the team. The pathway, the staff, the players, everything about it, it's just top. I'm excited to meet the group, meet the players, hit the ground running and have a good season."

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard sends transfer message to Liverpool over player they 'should have kept'
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard sends transfer message to Liverpool over player they 'should have kept'

Steven Gerrard spoke about Neco Williams before Liverpool snatched a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard spoke out on a player Liverpool sold (Image: (Oli SCARFF / AFP via Getty Images))

Steven Gerrard has told Liverpool they made a mistake selling Neco Williams to Nottingham Forest four years ago. Williams joined Forest from Liverpool in July 2022 for a fee of £12m and has made over 150 appearances for the club.

‌



Gerrard managed Williams at the youth team level at Liverpool, and the two were reunited ahead of the Reds’ 2-2 Premier League draw against Forest at Anfield on Saturday. And asked if he recognised what a talent Williams was at the time, Gerrard said: "I did actually, and I told him.

‌



“I told his parents they had an incredible talent and an incredible human being. He's an example to any young boy chasing a dream. He wanted it to be here at Liverpool initially but he got the setback that he had to move.

‌



"What he's done is grabbed that opportunity with both hands. He's grown, he's evolved and he's arguably one of the best full-backs in the league in my opinion."

As Williams praised the influence Gerrard had on him as a youngster, Gerrard interjected, adding: "I don't want to cut him off but this is a player that trains how he plays. He comes in of a morning, he does everything right, he's very professional. He's a winner, very aggressive, he's a competitor and we already know he has got the talent.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"If you put everything around your talent, you can play at this level and you can stay at this level. I still think he hasn't reached his ceiling yet. I think he's at an age where he can go to the next level with experience and more time and more games.

"He's playing out of position, doing an incredible job on the left side. Can you imagine what he'd be like on the right side? For me, he's a fantastic full-back.

"I'm not just saying it, and I apologise to the Forest fans, but Liverpool should have kept him."

‌



View 2 Images Steven Gerrard lavished praise on Neco Williams (Image: ( Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

Williams is in talks over a new deal at the City Ground, but a number of Forest's top-flight rivals are keen on the 25-year-old. Manchester United and Newcastle United are among those claimed to be interested in the Wales international.

But when asked about transfer speculation, Williams told TNT Sports: "You're trying to stitch me up there. Listen, every day I'm focused on the badge I'm wearing right now.

Article continues below

"Of course, it's nice to see that there's interest and teams showing interest, but I'm a Nottingham Forest player and fully focused on what I'm doing here. Every day is showing full commitment and giving my best to help this team."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola fumes at officials and Alisson SMASHES board after Liverpool controversy
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola fumes at officials and Alisson SMASHES board after Liverpool controversy

Liverpool were angry with fourth official Tim Robinson because he didn't have the substitution boards ready in time for a triple change and Nottingham Forest subsequently scored

View 4 Images Andoni Iraola criticised the officials post-match (Image: TNT Sports)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has questioned the professionalism of the fourth official after a controversial incident in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest.

‌



Victor Munoz's late strike earned a point for Liverpool in Saturday's early kick-off at Anfield after a chaotic game. Iraola was honest about his side's poor performance in the first half, but also raged at the officials, who he felt may have inadvertently benefited Forest.

‌



The Liverpool boss had been trying to make a triple substitution in the build-up to Forest's second goal, which came via Morgan Gibbs-White from the penalty spot after Alisson fouled Neco Williams in the box. But fourth official Tim Robinson didn't have the substitution boards ready in time, meaning Forest were able to take a quick throw-in and catch Liverpool off guard.

‌



Alisson dived in at Williams' feet, fouling the Forest wingback and Gibbs-White scored the spot-kick to make it 2-1. Iraola was seen shouting at Robinson while he attempted to get the numbers on the boards and the Spaniard hasn't cooled down in his post-match interview.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"I will analyse the penalty, yes, but a professional fourth official cannot take three minutes for the subs," Iraola told TNT Sports.

‌



"We gave the subs two or three minutes before. I was angry because in the previous stop we couldn’t make it. And before the throw-in I said 'let’s do it now', but I don’t know how to explain it but it has taken ages to prepare two boards."

Alisson was furious with the penalty decision and was booked for his protestations to referee Sam Barrott. The veteran goalkeeper was still seething at full-time, too, and was seen kicking one of the substitution boards, smashing a hole in it.

View 4 Images Tim Robinson didn't have the boards ready to make the triple change (Image: TNT Sports)

‌



Former Premier League referee Graham Scott wrote on X: "The subs boards are not fit for purpose. Each number has to be entered manually, and they only count up one at a time. Entering number 38 on its own could take several seconds and there are six numbers to plug in here.

"Also, the sponsors’ advertising makes them heavy and unwieldy, which is why the 4th has them on the ground. In UEFA comps the clubs have to enter the numbers themselves, which means they can get the subs done quicker. The PL only did this during Covid.

"The 4th official would have had to check and double check the names and numbers of all six players involved in the substitutions against the official team sheet in case the club has made an error, which happens frequently enough to make such checks necessary."

‌



4 View 4 Images The damaged substitutes board after Alisson's kick 4 View 4 Images Alisson was furious with the penalty call (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

The draw was Liverpool's second in succession to start the 2026/27 campaign following the 2-2 draw against Newcastle last weekend. Dan Ndoye put Forest ahead after Liverpool failed to deal with a long ball.

‌



Alexander Isak equalised with a tap-in from Cody Gakpo's cross before the penalty put the away side ahead once more. Munoz then earned Liverpool a point in the 82nd minute with a powerful shot off the underside of the crossbar.

"It’s not the result we want. I think two very different halves," Iraola said. "I think we were poor in the first half, even being poor, we were unlucky in terms of their goal.

"We were very poor in the first half. We were much better in the second half. The intensity was different - if you are going to lose, you have to lose like in the second half. A lot more intense, more threatening, happy with the second half, but it was late in the game."

Sports.title: Chaotic Liverpool come from behind twice to draw with Nottingham Forest - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Chaotic Liverpool come from behind twice to draw with Nottingham Forest - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-2 NOTTINGHAM FOREST: Victor Munoz's powerful effort in the 82nd minute sees the home side show spirit but no control in an engrossing match at Anfield

View 5 Images Victor Munoz smashed in a second equaliser for Liverpool (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Liverpool came from behind twice for the second time in a week to earn a point in an entertaining draw with Nottingham Forest which showed all the flaws Andoni Iraola needs to address. The Reds drew 2-2 against Newcastle on Sunday and followed it up with another 2-2 thanks to Victor Munoz's rocket.

‌



Dan Ndoye put Forest in front with a controlled finish into the bottom corner after Liverpool failed to deal with a long ball straight down the pitch. Florian Wirtz thought he'd equalised with a low shot on the spin, only for VAR to confirm that Jeremie Frimpong had been offside in the build-up. It was then nearly 2-0 to Forest, only for Alisson to produce a stunning save to keep out Igor Jesus.

‌



Anfield was showing plenty of frustration when, out of the blue, Alexander Isak tapped in a perfect back-post cross from Cody Gakpo on the hour-mark. The good times didn't last for the home side, with Morgan Gibbs-White making it 2-1 from the penalty spot after Alisson tripped Neco Williams following a quick throw-in.

‌



Liverpool bounced back again, however, when Munoz spun on Wirtz's line-splitting pass and smashed a powerful effort in via the underside of the crossbar. Here are the talking points.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Jacquet enters the chaos

The opening stages at Anfield saw Jeremy Jacquet at the forefront of the action. Liverpool's new centre-back started well, blocking two shots and clearing another dangerous ball, before it all went wrong.

It was the £55million signing who played Igor Jesus onside from Matz Sels's long kick. He then got attracted to the ball, leaving Ndoye free on the edge of the box, with right-back Frimpong and right winger Cody Gakpo nowhere to be seen. Wearing the No.5 shirt previously occupied by compatriot Ibrahima Konate, there were similarly chaotic vibes coming from the Liverpool defence.

View 5 Images Jeremy Jacquet couldn't prevent Dan Ndoye's goal (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

‌



Isak off the boil - then scores

This was supposed to be the season that Alexander Isak began to repay his £125million transfer fee. The 2025/26 campaign was impacted by a non-existent pre-season (of his own making) and injuries. But there are no longer any plausible excuses. It's time to deliver.

The Swede suffered a fractured ankle and fibula in December and for the first 60 minutes the worries grew over whether he will ever return to his red-hot Newcastle form. There were no promising signs initially, with Isak brushed off the ball by Jair Cunha in a 50/50 and otherwise largely anonymous, right up until Gakpo put a goal on a plate for him.

View 5 Images Alexander Isak scored a tap-in to make it 1-1 (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Glasner blueprint clear

Oliver Glasner has brought his favoured tactical system with him to Forest and their wingback-focused play was evident at Anfield. Ola Aina and Williams are well-suited to the wingback position, but it was James McAtee who caught the eye and controlled things in the middle of the pitch.

McAtee joined Forest from Manchester City last summer for a fee which could reach £30m and appears set to benefit from the departure of Elliot Anderson in the opposite direction. The diminutive midfielder is at his best with the ball at his feet and showed plenty of nice touches to claim the TNT Sports' man of the match award.

Gakpo has to stay

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo has shown his value this season already (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

‌



Gakpo has become a divisive player among Liverpool fans, but he's shown his worth already this season, rifling a long-range goal in at St James' Park last weekend before setting up the Isak goal here.

Gakpo has transfer attention from Manchester City and Tottenham and his future is up in the air ahead of the 11pm deadline on Tuesday night. Liverpool may have agreed a £123m deal for Bradley Barcola, but Munoz and Rio Ngumoha could do with keeping Gakpo as a teammate.

Iraola short of firepower

View 5 Images Morgan Gibbs-White made it 2-1 from the penalty spot (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

‌



Iraola made all five substitutions while chasing the game in the second half. On came Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas, Ryan Gravenberch, Ronald Araujo and Trey Nyoni. Hardly the cavalry: two defenders, two holding midfielders and one young winger. The changes also saw Dominik Szoboszlai shifted to right-back in a head-scratching alteration. Thankfully, Munoz's rocket spared blushes for the second straight weekend.

There is some understanding that things will take time for the former Bournemouth boss to make his mark after taking over from Arne Slot. But right now it is not looking good, with problems all over the pitch and not much time left in the transfer window to change it.

Sports.title: Fery's dreams of maiden ATP Tour title ended in Winston-Salem Open final
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery's hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title at Winston-Salem Open was ended in emphatic fashion by Peruvian Ignacio Buse on Saturday.

From 3-3 in the first set, Fery lost six straight games before eventually going down 6-3 6-2 to Buse.

The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.

Fery was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon and he is set for a new career high Monday.

With his spot in the Winston-Salem final, 24-year-old Fery has moved up to a new career high of No 33 in the live rankings, overtaking Cameron Norrie as the British No 1 in doing so.

Eight weeks ago, Fery was outside the top 100.

"Congratulations to you and your team, Ignacio, for your second title this year," Fery said during the trophy ceremony. "I want to thank my team as well. It couldn't be us today but thank you for everything you do for me. We have had a great year and hopefully we can finish strong."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery reflects on his Wimbledon experience and his massive climb up the world rankings

Speaking to Sky Sports, former British No 1 Tim Henman said he has been impressed with Fery's showing in North Carolina.

Fery, who is set to make his main draw debut at the US Open starting on Sunday, faces a tough task against Italy's world No 14 Lorenzo Musetti in the opening round.

"He's had a great week, but that's his level," said Henman. "On the back of making the semi-finals at Wimbledon, he's a top 30 player, so getting through to the final of tour events and hopefully winning them is what he's about now.

"Yes, he has a tough match against Musetti. He goes into that match as a clear underdog but he's confident."

Buse delivered a composed performance to secure his triumph in just 77 minutes, with Fery unable to match the relentless pace.

"It is very special for me," Buse said in his post-match interview. "With all my team, we have been working very, very hard. Some things are very tough that we go through as tennis players, but I also want to congratulate Arthur and his team."

Sports.title: Hovland leads Scheffler in FedExCup thriller as McIlroy makes late push
Sports.content:
Viktor Hovland takes a one-shot lead into the final round of the Tour Championship, as Scottie Scheffler stayed in contention and Rory McIlroy kept his FedExCup hopes alive.

Hovland produced a birdie-birdie finish to post a five-under 65 at East Lake, lifting the 2023 FedExCup champion to 15 under and with a narrow advantage over playing partner Ryan Gerard.

The halfway co-leaders were chased down by a star-studded chasing pack during a thrilling Saturday at the PGA Tour's season finale, with world no 1 Scottie Scheffler three shots back in third spot and chasing a second FedExCup title.

Scheffler is joined on 12 under by Chris Gotterup, Adam Scott and Ludvig Åberg, who produced a three-birdie finish to his third-round 65, as McIlroy jumped to tied-seventh after setting the early clubhouse target with a round-of-the-day 63.

McIlroy sits five strokes back alongside Cameron Young as he searches for a record-extending fourth FedExCup title, with all 29 players in the field under-par heading into the final round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy reflects on charging up the leaderboard with a third-round 63 at East Lake

How Hovland edged ahead in FedExCup battle

Gotterup quickly made it a three-way tie with a birdie at the third, as Hovland - playing with Gerard - took advantage of the same hole but failed to get up and down from the sand to save par at the next.

Young birdied two of his first six holes to also get to 10 under, while McIlroy charged through the field and made four birdies in a six-hole stretch in his back nine to increase the logjam for the lead.

Image: Cameron Young had charged up the leaderboar with a round-of-the-day 62 on Friday

McIlroy had been eight back earlier in his round but set the clubhouse target, moments before Gotterup briefly claimed the solo lead, before Hovland and Gerard both took advantage of the par-five sixth to edge ahead on 11 under.

Gerard added another birdie from nine feet at the seventh and traded pars with Hovland around the turn, before doubling his advantage over a congested chasing pack by holing from 12 feet at the 12th.

Image: Ryan Gerard has previously only won once on the PGA Tour at last year's Barracuda Championship

Hovland converted from a similar distance to birdie the next and nailed a 15-footer to match Gerard's par at the 14th, then picked up a shot at the 15th to pull level with his playing partner on 13 under.

Both players saved par at the 16th and Hovland claimed the outright lead with an eight-foot birdie at the 17th, before the pair traded birdies at the par-five last to ensure they would go out in the last group again on Sunday.

"Super pleased," Hovland said. "65 out there, especially with that finish, I'm super happy with that. I'd say the last few weeks I have been putting a lot better, but it's been hard to put together consistently good days in a row. It's been just one of those weeks where I've been able to put it together every single day for three days.

McIlroy fights back to stay in FedExCup mix

The Masters champion was seven off the halfway lead and showed little sign of a title push when he scrambled a par at the first and made a three-putt bogey at the second, only to birdie his next two holes and take advantage of the par-five sixth.

Image: Rory McIlroy has previously won the FedExCup in 2016, 2019 and 2022

McIlroy added another from 10 feet at the par-four seventh but failed to take advantage of the driveable eighth, then saw a close-range birdie at the 10th cancelled out by a dropped shot at the next.

The world No 2 picked up a shot from eight feet at the 12th and holed three birdie chances of 12 feet on longer in consecutive holes from the 15th, seeing him equal his lowest career round at East Lake.

Image: Rory McIlroy's nine birdies equalled his most in a round this season on the PGA Tour

"I got myself back in the tournament," McIlroy said. "I think the difference today was I just putted a lot better. I think I lost maybe a combined three (shots) on the greens over the first two days and I probably gained over three on the greens today.

"The ball striking has been there. Hit some nice iron shots, drove it well for the most part. I felt like I played okay the last couple days, just wasn't getting as much out of my game as I wanted to. I pieced it together today and obviously with a better score."

Sports.title: Cameron calls for three-minute round rematch as Mayer disputes result
Sports.content:
Chantelle Cameron has called for a three-minute-round rematch against Mikaela Mayer after beating the American by unanimous decision to become the unified WBA, WBC and WBO super-welterweight champion at MVPW-06 in Birmingham.

The Brit clinched an unrelenting contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges' scorecards to underscore her status among the all-time greats of female boxing.

Cameron's rivalry with Mayer took a twist this week after a physical altercation and fierce war of words at their weigh-in resulted in them having to be split by security - and the new unified world champion has left the door open to a second instalment of their chapter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron reflects on her victory over Mikaela Mayer and bites back at Mayer's antics in the build up to the fight.

"She wanted the weight, she wanted the twos [two-minute rounds], she wanted to have her name first, which is actually fine because we're not going to get into that," said Cameron in her post-fight press conference.

"If we want the rematch we have to do three-minute rounds. I'll speak to my team, I would like to do three-minute rounds, if it means vacating the WBC belt again I don't mind doing that."

Cameron, the only woman to beat Katie Taylor in the Irish great's professional career, put Saturday night's result to the top of her resume but downplayed suggestions she is now the greatest female boxer of all time.

"I'll say it's my best win, I really enjoyed it tonight," she said. "I still think Claressa Shields is the best, I won't be deluded, Mikaela would, but Claressa is still No 1."

Tensions had boiled over on the eve of their fight as Cameron and Mayer clashed during a fiery weigh-in, an altercation the eventual victor believes worked in her favour come fight night.

"I think it she messed up, I think maybe it was too nicey nicey and friendly," said Cameron. "I did genuinely respect her. I was a fan of her. But the way she's coming on, I just think she's made a bit of a fool of herself.

"I knew that. I was looking at her before the bell rang and thought, I'm gonna smash your head in. And I think it worked.

"I was feeling the energy she didn't want to be in there, I could feel it."

Image: Cameron withstood significant damage to the right eye to secure the win

The pair would later clash again following the final bell as Mayer disputed the decision, Cameron insisting any rematch would need to take place on her terms.

"I just wanted to play with [Mayer]," Cameron told Sky Sports after the fight. "If you're going to say you'll stop me, beat me easily... talk is so cheap, and I showed that tonight [Saturday]. Don't talk too much game - you've got to back it

"I want to do this again. It's up to Mikaela, but I want to do three-minute rounds.

"I'll speak to my team and see if Mikaela wants it, but - [to Mayer] - didn't you say you were going to beat me so bad that I wasn't going to want a rematch?"

The British boxer continued to goad her opponent, adding: "You were talking so much nonsense I actually fell asleep for a second!

"Three-minute rounds, let's do it.

"Go back to the gym, work on your power, work on your fitness, work on your speed, work on your boxing - make some improvements, because your team aren't doing a great job are they!

"You're boring - go home!"

Mayer disputes result and pushes for rematch in USA

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The supposed friendship between Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron looks to be over following a fiery clash where they butted heads and swapped furious words.

Mayer disputed the judges' decision after her defeat, claiming she "outboxed" Cameron on her own turf:

"I did beat you Chantelle. You are lucky in your little back yard.

"You can have your re-match. Three-minute rounds. If you want to vacate your WBC belt you can do that. It's your prerogative now. I'll just kick your ass even harder.

"But it won't be here. It won't be in the UK. If you want to come to the US you can.

"I outboxed you. I'll go back and rewatch it and give an honest evaluation, but I just beat you.

"If the public says I'm wrong you can have that... my initial feeling is I outboxed her."

Shields an option?

MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian welcomed a second meeting between Cameron and Mayer, while also pointing towards marquee names elsewhere at the top of the sport.

"I think Chantelle said it, she'd like to do the rematch, she'd like to sit down with the WBC and do three minute rounds. it's where she wants to be," Bidarian told reporters.

"She has said to us from the jump she would like to fight Claressa Shields and from the jump said she would like to fight Lauren Price, she's up for fighting anyone.

"Unequivocally, if she's not the GWOAT, she's one of the top two or three ever."

Three-minute rounds could lead to WBC belt vacation, says Moore

Image: Chantelle Cameron celebrates after beating Mikaela Mayer

Cameron's coach, Jamie Moore, says there is a possibility that Cameron could vacate the WBC title if they don't allow her to stage a three-minute round title defence against Mayer.

"I think in general, Chantelle is much better over three minutes.

"There's an issue with the WBC, and Chantelle is going to speak to her team to see if she might vacate the belt.

"Chantelle is adamant that - for female boxing moving forward - to be on the same level as men's boxing, it's got to be three-minute rounds."

Sports.title: Hrgovic stuns Itauma with epic comeback as Brit loses unbeaten record
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic produced one of the shocks of the boxing year, stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2 to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title and become Croatia's first world heavyweight champion.

Itauma, unbeaten coming into the fight and one of the sport's most talked about young talents, had started like a man intent on an early night and for six rounds barely lost a minute.

It looked like Itauma's bid to become Britain's second-youngest world champion was on course for success after a right hook to the temple rocked Hrgovic inside the opening minute, followed by a second-round left hook that forced the Croatian to steady himself with a glove on the canvas.

Itauma had won every round heading into the second half of the fight but that wasn't telling the full story.

Everything Itauma landed, including a fifth-round left uppercut detonated flush on the point of the chin, was absorbed by a man who had been in the deep waters before, and the effort of trying to move the immovable was draining the younger man with every round he banked.

The seventh round took Itauma beyond six rounds for the first time in his career, and the eighth broke him. Sensing his chance, he emptied the tank in a sustained assault, but Hrgovic stood firm and absorbed the punishment, leaving the young challenger almost completely spent.

Within a minute of the ninth Itauma was out on his feet, unable to hold himself steady as Hrgovic came forward, and his corner threw the towel with their man defenceless. He was attended by medical staff in his corner afterwards having given everything he had.

"Let me ask my young friend something," enquired Hrgovic. "Is a chin important? Chin is important.

"He's an amazing fighter – I want to thank him. To give me a chance to become a new superstar in the heavyweight division. I am the present. He is definitely the future.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind.

"From the first round, I saw him gassing out. He started fast, I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came, I needed to push. That is what I did."

For Hrgovic, it was the defining win of a long career, as his toughness and experience in boxing's hardest rooms were rewarded on a night when almost every scoring shot went against him. The victory also reshapes the heavyweight title picture, with the IBF belt now in Croatian hands.

For Itauma, a first professional defeat arrives as a brutal education rather than a humiliation, beaten not by a bigger puncher but by the questions of pace, patience and endurance that his early blowouts had never asked.

Sports.title: De Zerbi highlights biggest problem at Spurs as Carra slams 'worst start'
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi believes changing the mentality at Tottenham is his biggest challenge after Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher said their start to the season "couldn't have gone any worse" following defeat to Newcastle.

Tottenham have lost their first two Premier League games without scoring a goal and sit at the bottom of the league despite spending £320m in the transfer market this summer.

De Zerbi's side had been better than Newcastle until Anthony Elanga struck the opener midway through the second half, with Spurs unable to respond and conceding another when Yoane Wissa hooked in from close range.

Asked whether mentality was the biggest issue he faces, De Zerbi said: "You are right, yes. It's the biggest problem, it's the biggest challenge, the biggest target is to find the right mentality.

"Unfortunately you can't buy the mentality in the transfer market. Football is like magic: you can change many players in one window of the transfer market, and you can find the balance immediately, or you need more time. I would like to achieve this target quickly, as soon as possible, because it's crucial to play football.

"But the plan, the project of the club, what we are doing to rebuild a new team with new players, is a great plan, is a great project, and I have no doubt about the result of this project."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Tottenham and Newcastle

De Zerbi reinforced his belief that this season would be different to Spurs' previous two, which have seen them finish 17th in the past two seasons.

He said: "I'm disappointed with the result, and I'm sorry for the fans, for the environment, because after two defeats, maybe somebody can think it's the same story, the same as the last two seasons. I have no doubt it's not like this. I can't change my opinion for two defeats.

"I have big, big confidence in the qualities of my players. At the end, when we become a team, when we improve the connection between the players, when we improve the quality of the play, when we improve the defensive space, this group, with me or with another coach, nothing changes, because they are two good players.

"I'm sorry for the club, because they are building a great squad, but maybe now we are not ready yet, for many, many reasons."

'Tottenham will go into market again'

Sky Sports' Carragher said on co-commentary at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium that he reckons Spurs will sign another player after their poor start.

"Tottenham's start to the season couldn't have gone any worse," he said. "But it's going to take time at Tottenham. A lot of new players have come in; they've paid top dollar, but they're quality players, certainly in the midfield area, like [Mateus] Fernandes and [Sandro] Tonali.

"We saw signs today in terms of [Jan Paul] Van Hecke on the ball, but it won't be finished. I think there will be more to come.

"It's natural that people will panic a little and Tottenham will go into the market again, there's no doubt about it.

"Not just because they've lost twice, but it makes you more decisive. If you've won both games and a couple of games and some of the players looked alright, you'd look at a couple of deals and think 'maybe we're OK, maybe we give those players until Christmas'.

"That certainly won't be the case on the back of two really bad defeats."

'Spurs project will take time'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp blamed Tottenham captain Micky van de Ven for 'jogging back' when Anthony Elanga was closing in on Newcastle's opening goal

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp called for patience on Saturday Night Football.

"There's a lot of new players at Spurs and it's going to take time," he said. "The manager has got a jigsaw puzzle and he's got to figure out how to fit the players in, what system to use, who the best three players are in midfield.

"There are going to be teething problems. I also look at the senior players and players like [Micky] Van de Ven didn't do enough to lead today and certainly with the goals.

"Players who have been there for a long time can do better."

Sports.title: Lavish spending fails to fix Tottenham’s big issue – the lack of soul and spine | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Time for Tottenham to start panicking? This is, of course, a subtle trick question. Tottenham is one of those clubs that never actually stops panicking. They panic when they concede and they panic when they score. They panic when they have the ball and they panic when someone else does. They have a coach in Roberto De Zerbi whose face evokes a state of permanent alarm, the expression of a man perpetually having a toilet door opened on him. One year they even managed to panic their way to the Europa League. For the ever-rattled Spurs fan, this club is less a treasured devotion and more a lifelong haunting, broken up by occasional panic substitutions.

You could intuit that sense of encrusted resignation pretty much from the moment Anthony Elanga’s improvised shot kissed the post and trickled over the line to give Newcastle the lead. Since beating Aston Villa 4-1 in late 2024, Tottenham have gone behind 44 times in all competitions and come back to win precisely zero of them. There is something innate and endemic here, a chronic case of Long Tottenham for which – despite the new coach, the new leadership structure and more than a third of a billion pounds in transfer fees – there remains no proven cure. Yoane Wissa’s clincher was of zero surprise to anyone.

And so welcome back to the temple of pain, the Theatre of Everyone Else’s Dreams, a stadium that fittingly still has no naming rights because pretty much every visiting side gets to own the place. Over the past 12 months, Aston Villa have won the same number of domestic fixtures at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (two) as Tottenham. Unai Emery’s men may well get the chance to retake their lead here in three weeks’ time. In the meantime it was Newcastle, with one clean sheet in their last 18 matches, who feasted on Tottenham’s neuroses, stayed tight and stayed patient, waited for the train that always arrives.

Perhaps as Matthias Jaissle’s team climbed all over the duels and the second balls there was also a certain reassuring symbolism here: a lesson in the enduring value of culture over commerce. Newcastle have lost half a team but kept their soul; Tottenham have bought half a team and are still searching for theirs. There were inevitable boos for Sandro Tonali, who was actually fine: one of those rare Tottenham players who actually treasures the ball and wants to do interesting things with it. Alongside him Mateus Fernandes was restless, classy, excellent. Omar Marmoush on his debut looked fit and sharp. But of course the individuals were never the problem here.

View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali tussles with Anthony Elanga. Photograph: Neil Hall/EPA

The problem was the little things: the lost headers, the fractional pauses on the ball that kill momentum, the rushed shots, the extra touches, the tackles not quite committed to, the barely perceptible signs of a deep-rooted softness. Take Elanga’s goal, which sprang from an unpressed Nico González long ball, a poorly challenged Amar Dedic header, a cool turn and finish. Three very simple things in a row, at least two of which should probably have been prevented. No screaming howler or smoking gun here. Just a run of lost battles, a sum of marginal flaws, a team that for all its moments of promise and competence has not yet been welded together into a coherent whole.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

How De Zerbi fixes this is anyone’s guess. It feels increasingly clear that for all the new blood there is still a kind of generational trauma here, perhaps dating back to the injury crisis of 2024-25, when a threadbare squad was pushed beyond the boundaries of wellness and sanity. For the veterans of that campaign, your Archie Grays and Micky van de Vens, your Destiny Udogies and Rodrigo Bentancurs, you occasionally glimpse that accumulated tension in the 50-50 tackles and big physical clashes, the sense of players still not quite trusting their bodies. And oppositions really do pick up on this stuff. Right now there is a clear blueprint for beating Tottenham: compete, do the simple things well, and eventually bully them into playing your game.

How much worse does this get before it gets better? Are Spurs fans ultimately in for another season of discontent and disgruntlement, of taking an unhealthy interest in the latest score from the Coventry Building Society Arena? The instinct here is still to be patient and wait for the required chemistry to develop. But what if two defeats become four, or six? What if it’s November and the top scorer is still somehow Richarlison with two? How does a club so medicinally addicted to panic possibly avoid it?

Quietly, there is now some ridiculous creative talent at this club. The signings of Marmoush and Sávio, the new-look midfield, the return of Mohammed Kudus and Dominic Solanke, the prospect of James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski and Xavi Simons to come. A World Cup finalist in Marcos Senesi sitting unused on the bench. It feels inconceivable that Tottenham could be in relegation trouble again. But as with so many clubs before them, Tottenham are discovering that buying new footballers is the easy part. Growing a spine will take considerably longer.

Sports.title: Liverpool’s Andoni Iraola angered by substitution delay before Forest penalty
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola bemoaned a poor first-half display plus a broken electronic board for Liverpool’s disappointing 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest in the first home game of his Anfield reign. Forest led twice, but were denied a third successive Premier League win at Liverpool by Víctor Muñoz’s emphatic 82nd-minute equaliser.

The visitors’ second goal, from a penalty converted by Morgan Gibbs-White, stemmed from a throw-in taken quickly by Liam Delap while Iraola was attempting to make a triple substitution.

He was prevented from doing so because the fourth official was unable to flash up the substitutes’ numbers due to a malfunctioning electronic board. “I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” said the exasperated Liverpool head coach.

“I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. It was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. He [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board. The penalty wouldn’t have happened if I had made the subs.

“I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. I’ll leave you to decide whether it was a penalty or not.”

Despite his annoyance over the buildup to Forest’s penalty, Iraola conceded that Liverpool created their own problems for the second week in succession with a sluggish start.

He said: “The first half was poor, it was not good enough. We haven’t controlled the game and after we improved a lot in the second half. We were much more intense, quicker on the ball and had more urgency, but it hasn’t been enough to win the game and we have to blame the first half.

“I am frustrated because we want to win, especially at home. It’s not a good result. We have come back from two results where we were losing and I like what we have done in the second half, but we haven’t been able to complete the comeback.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In the first half we were too passive without the ball. Afterwards we improved this and intensity gives you the chance to win duels and attack quicker and better. But in the first half there was a lack of intensity and we had issues with throw-ins today.”

Sports.title: Carrick dismisses ‘lazy’ Manchester United criticism and defends Fernandes’ leadership
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has said it was “lazy and easy” to say everything was wrong with Manchester United after the opening-day defeat at Hull.

United lost 2-0 in a tame display and the manager was asked whether his captain, Bruno Fernandes, and Youri Tielemans, Belgium’s captain, had shown the leadership that might have affected the performance and result.

“It’s one game,” Carrick said. “I think there’s enough leadership in our dressing room that we’ll have it throughout the season. Just because we lose a game doesn’t just mean leadership [is the reason]. I got ‘passion’ thrown at me after the game; it’s not just that. You lose two set plays like we did [for the goals], it changes the game.”

Carrick was asked what the reason was for the performance. “You’ve watched football a long time, right? Teams lose games and win games, and it’s not just because you try or you don’t try. There’s all sorts of different reasons. I don’t have to give you the total reason, because we know what we’re trying to improve on.”

The 45-year-old was pressed to offer one factor why the defeat occurred. “I think it’s so easy and lazy to just … a team loses a game, everything’s wrong: this is wrong, this is wrong, not trying enough, not enough passion,” Carrick said. “It’s like the obvious answer. So, there’s a lot that goes into a game of football that can take [the result away] from [you].

“We’ve probably played like that and won games, and everyone goes: ‘What a great team, what a great coach, what a great load of players’ – when we find a way to win 1-0. So, from my perspective, when you’re analysing it, it’s not the feeling [that the inverse is true]. We’ve got to dig deeper than that and understand the details of it. And we don’t get carried away when we win certain games because we know it’s not been perfect.”

United host Ipswich on Sunday without Carlos Baleba, who signed on Tuesday for £70m from Brighton but has an ankle injury that may rule him out for three or more weeks. This means the midfielder may not make his debut until Tottenham’s visit on 10 October, after the international break.

United have admired the Cameroon international since last summer so Carrick was asked why the 22-year-old was signed so late in the window. He said: “It’s not always straightforward, and things have got to drop. So we’ve been patient. We wanted to get the right players in, that fit the group, that will take us forward, and Carlos is definitely one of them.”

Sports.title: No country for old men: Premier League grind is why managers are getting younger
Sports.content:
One of the problems with getting older is that you’re never quite sure whether it’s you or them. Is the world really changing, or is it just you, struggling to adapt? There’s a milestone in life, probably as you’re contemplating university or a first job, when you realise you’re watching a footballer who is younger than you. Then, 15-20 years later, you realise you’re watching a manager who is younger than you. And 15-20 years after that, especially if you’re watching the modern Premier League, you realise that almost every manager is younger than you.

At which you do two things: give thanks for David Moyes; and check to see whether it’s actually happening, or whether this is just the football equivalent of the policemen-getting-younger cliche.

It turns out it is true. Managers used to be ashen-faced men with nicotine-grey hair dressed in the sports jackets of grim experience. They spoke with a rasping melancholy of the depths of human fallibility and of fates that were not to be trusted. Now they’re trim, sprightly figures in T-shirts, convinced that analytics can explain the world.

There are fewer Premier League managers now aged 50 or over than at any point in the past 20 years: only four, and two of those have only just made it over the threshold. Moyes is 63 (three months younger than José Mourinho, which, like Aberdeen being further west than Bristol, is a fact both true and too counterintuitive to be worth believing). Then there is Unai Emery at 54, Oliver Glasner at 52 and Régis Le Bris at 50. Most Premier League managers are in their 40s, with the youngest two Matthias Jaissle, 38, and Fabian Hürzeler, 33.

This is not coincidence; rather it seems the result of two interconnected trends. Even at the turn of the century, when Mourinho was starting out, it was unusual for a manager not to have played the game to at least a reasonable level, which meant they were starting their managerial careers in their mid-thirties. That’s still the route many take – Andoni Iraola, Michael Carrick, Gary O’Neil or Álvaro Arbeloa, for instance.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola’s first appointment as head coach was at AEK Larnaca in 2018, aged 35. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

But there’s also a recognition, to use Arrigo Sacchi’s phrase, that a jockey does not need first to have been a horse. Coaching is regarded as a job in its own right, requiring a very different skillset to playing. Hürzeler came through the youth systems at Bayern Munich, Hoffenheim and 1860 Munich but, aged 22, in part because of an ankle injury, decided to focus on coaching.

Jaissle was a member of the Hoffenheim side that soared through the divisions to win promotion to the Bundesliga before knee and achilles tendon injuries ended his playing career at 26. The early switch into coaching seems particularly common in Germany: Thomas Tuchel and Julian Nagelsmann have similar stories.

That greater receptiveness to career coaches explains the wave of younger managers. But there are also fewer older coaches.

In part it may be coincidence: an experienced generation – Sam Allardyce, Tony Pulis and Alan Pardew – grew old together. That the process occurred just as many of their tactical characteristics – low blocks, direct play, a focus on set pieces – re-entered the mainstream may not simply be irony. The old must be cast out before it is reinvented as new; the modish cannot be represented by a 60-something football man.

But it’s also because modern management is exhausting. At Ipswich, Kieran McKenna would have his coaches present their plans to him for the day at 6am, altering anything he felt wasn’t quite right. That plan would be sent to the staff at the training ground to set up all the various pitches and drills. McKenna would then go to check everything was laid out properly. It was all extraordinarily detailed; everything was marked out, down to where players should stand when they weren’t directly involved and where water bottles would be placed.

During sessions, McKenna would walk between each unit, stepping in to offer advice and make amendments. After sessions, coaches would watch them back and report to McKenna on what could be improved before planning the next day’s drills to be presented at 6am the following morning.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Kieran McKenna’s relentless coaching at Ipswich was exhausting so it was no surprise he needed a break following their third promotion in five years. Photograph: Cat Goryn/Action Images/Reuters

During 11 v 11 practice games, McKenna would be the only one who coached. Over his five years at Ipswich, no drill was ever repeated in exactly the same form; repetition and possible staleness were to be avoided at all costs. Little wonder that after a third promotion in five seasons at the club, he felt exhausted, in need of a break rather than taking on an uneven fight in an ungrateful Premier League that could only sap his reserves further.

Brian Clough would take holidays during the season. He would turn up only infrequently at training. His input was sharp, erratic, impressionistic. Four decades on, a top-level manager is running a team of coaches and analysts that probably outnumbers the players with whom he has direct contact.

He cannot simply ignore the board until he needs money for a signing but has to manage up to whatever structure of sporting directors exists above him. He often will have little autonomy, although the success of Mikel Arteta, who has a more traditional role and seems to micromanage everything at Arsenal, may change that. And he is liable to be sacked after a month of poor form. The pressure is enormous, the margin for error minute.

That perhaps explains why so many top managers are now drifting into international football. Management, it’s commonly said, is a drug, but perhaps that fix is more palatable when it is delivered in five doses spread over a season, plus a major tournament every other year, rather than in the relentless drudgery of the club game. Carlo Ancelotti took his break from the club game at 66, Jürgen Klopp at 56, Tuchel at 50. None have demonstrated any great desire to return to the remorselessness of the league.

The Premier League may be the greatest stage in management. It may be where the best salaries are paid. It may be where every manager wishes to test himself. But it is an exhausting and capricious world that requires extraordinary reserves of energy, physical and mental. It is no theatre for old men.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Moyes wants to keep Armstrong while Forest agree Muñoz deal
Sports.content:
The sale of the 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest would be a “club decision” for Everton, according to David Moyes. After his team’s 1-1 draw at Bournemouth, in which Armstrong played the full 90 minutes, Moyes said he would prefer to keep a player for whom a reported £40m offer has been made.

“I know there’s been an offer, I don’t really think there’s much else I’ve got to say about it,” Moyes said, initially refusing to be drawn. “It’s not really a question for just now, it’ll be a club decision.”

Moyes has previously suggested his discomfort with a lack of business this summer, suggesting his squad was not big enough. His stance was unaltered here on Saturday. “I have said we could do with strengthening and hopefully we can do that. We have a good basis. Let’s hope we can build on it.

“I don’t think we can afford to lose any players, certainly not our better ones. The club dictates a lot of that and we will see how the next few days go.”

Travelling Everton fans sang that the club would have a “riot on your hands” should Armstrong be sold. Moyes, when asked about the supporters’ reaction, said: “I’d say the manager’s an Evertonian.”

He continued: “You always have to consider supporters. Supporters aren’t always wrong. But then there’s also times where I’ve fortunately had people at clubs who are really powerful and make difficult decisions.

“I’d bring into that Bryan Gray, who was at Preston North End, and also Sir Philip Carter, who was at Everton when I first came in. Not always decisions are popular, and sometimes they have to do it for different reasons. It’s like managers have to make decisions on players … but there’s sometimes bigger decisions to be made and the club will, I’m sure, make what they think is the right one.”

On the performance of Armstrong, the teenager lining up in midfield in a game where James Tarkowski’s injury-time goal was required to rescue a point, Moyes said: “Harrison played really well, he did a lot of good work. He ran out of legs a little bit later in the game, but it’s amazing the effort he puts in and he was probably more of an influence in the first half than he was in the second half.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Daniel Muñoz, meanwhile, will have a medical in the next few days after Nottingham Forest agreed a deal worth an initial £22m with Crystal Palace for the Colombia defender. The 30-year-old moved to Selhurst Park in 2024 under Oliver Glasner, who moved to the City Ground from Palace this summer.

Muñoz sat through Friday’s 4-1 home defeat by Manchester City on the bench as talks between the clubs continued. He had played in Pierre Sage’s first game in charge of Palace, the 2-0 defeat at Everton.

Sports.title: European football: Elversberg stun Leverkusen in dream Bundesliga debut
Sports.content:
The Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg began their first top-flight campaign in style, stunning Bayer Leverkusen with an impressive 3-2 home victory on Saturday.

Lukas Petkov and Cole Campbell scored within 60 seconds of each other to put Elversberg 2-0 up before the 10-minute mark. David Mokwa added another early in the second half in front of 9,307 delirious fans.

Patrik Schick and Christian Kofane pulled late goals back, but it was not enough to prevent a famous victory for Elversberg, as they embarrassed a team who won the title in 2024 without losing a game.

The town of Elversberg has a population of just 13,000, making it the smallest settlement to have ever hosted a Bundesliga side. Their ground, the Ursapharm-Arena, has a reduced capacity while upgrades are made to meet the German top flight’s stadium criteria.

“It’s an indescribable day,” the Elversberg captain, Lukas Pinckert, told Sky. “We worked hard to earn the right to play in this league. The victory is deserved. I am incredibly proud of the team.”

Leverkusen looked disorganised and lacked energy until late on, showing new coach Carles Martínez Novell that he has work to do. The Spaniard took over from Kasper Hjulmand in the summer after leaving his previous role at Ligue 1 side Toulouse.

RB Leipzig cruised to a 3-0 home win over Borussia Mönchengladbach, with the former Chelsea and France forward Christopher Nkunku setting up a goal on his return to the club.

Ridle Baku’s first-half goal came against the run of play for Leipzig but the hosts took control when Antonio Nusa produced a stunning finish early in the second half. Nkunku came on midway through the second half and set up a goal for the former Gladbach forward Rocco Reitz just two minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Antonio Nusa’s shot flies beyond Moritz Nicolas at the Red Bull Arena. Photograph: Ronny Hartmann/AFP/Getty Images

Union Berlin came from 3-1 down to draw 3-3 with Eintracht Frankfurt, cancelling out Younes Ebnoutalib’s hat-trick for the visitors. Union’s Tim Skarke scored in the third minute of stoppage time to level for the hosts.

The Cologne substitute Thijs Dallinga scored two goals and young winger Said El Mala scored a dazzling solo effort as the hosts came from behind twice to beat Hoffenheim 3-2. Elsewhere, Mainz played out a scoreless draw at home to promoted Paderborn.

Juventus saw off Parma 2-0 to make it back-to-back wins at the start of the Serie A season, while Fiorentina’s celebrations of the club’s 100th anniversary were spoilt by a 3-0 home defeat by promoted Frosinone.

Juve had to work hard for their three points, needing second-half goals from the substitutes Nicolás González and Teun Koopmeiners to secure the victory.

The close-season signings Randal Kolo Muani and Jhon Lucumi both started, while 18-year-old Bosnian Kerim Alajbegovic had an impact after coming off the bench to make his debut.

In Florence, club legends, including Gabriel Batistuta and Claudio Ranieri, were in attendance, only to see Fiorentina fail to bounce back from their 4-0 thrashing at Roma last weekend in their opener. Antonio Raimondo netted twice for the visitors, with Gabriele Bracaglia also on the scoresheet.

In Ligue 1, winger Gessime Yassine struck twice as Strasbourg came ⁠from behind to beat Lens 2-1 at home, ending the visitors’ ⁠strong start to ⁠the ​season. Lens took the lead when Jeyland Mitchell felled Abdallah Sima in the box, and captain Florian Thauvin stepped up to confidently rattle home the spot-kick in the 38th minute.

Strasbourg came out firing in the second half, equalising ​through a deflected Yassine strike after three minutes. The hosts had a goal ruled out for offside in the 56th minute, but grabbed a deserved late winner when Sebastian Nanasi ​crossed for ‌Yassine to volley home.

Atlético Madrid put the noise of the Julián Alvarez transfer saga behind them with a convincing 3-1 victory at Sevilla to move top of the early La Liga table. Diego Simeone’s men have taken seven points from their first three matches of the league season.

Atleti have repeatedly ruled out a move to Barcelona for Alvarez, who has also been heavily linked with Arsenal. The Argentina international was left out of the matchday squad in Seville, having been booed by his own fans last weekend in a 2-2 home draw with Villarreal.

The two forwards who started in his absence combined to great effect to give Atlético a fourth-minute lead. Lee Kang-in, a summer signing from Paris Saint-Germain, played an excellent pass in behind for Álex Baena to rifle a low shot into the net.

View image in fullscreen Álex Baena scores Atlético Madrid’s third goal at Sevilla. Photograph: Fran Santiago/Getty Images

The Rojiblancos doubled their advantage in the 26th minute, as Ademola Lookman planted a clever shot inside Odysseas Vlachodimos’s near post.

Atlético were three goals in front just seven minutes later as Spanish World Cup winner Baena scored his second. He drove a shot into the bottom corner from outside the box after being teed up by Marcos Llorente.

Sevilla improved in the second half and pulled one back through Miguel Sierra’s volley, but never looked like mounting a comeback.

Real Betis missed the chance to extend their perfect start, and briefly go top of La Liga, as they slumped to a 5-2 defeat at Levante. Dela broke the deadlock for the hosts with a glancing header, but centre-half Marc Bartra levelled quickly with a powerful strike from the edge of the penalty area.

Levante reclaimed the lead in first-half stoppage time, Enzo Bardeli lobbing Betis goalkeeper Álvaro Valles from long distance – only for Rodrigo Riquelme to equalise again from a corner before the break. Roger Brugué struck twice in the second half to put Levante in charge and a late Jon Ander Olasagasti header sealed the win.

Real Sociedad got their first points of the season with a 2-1 home win over Espanyol.

Sports.title: Hull maintain flying start as Liam Millar’s winner ruins Coventry’s day
Sports.content:
Perhaps last Saturday’s triumph was not a one-off. Hull backed up a shock victory against Manchester United by maintaining their 100% start to the Premier League and condemning Coventry to successive defeats. “We’re gonna win the league,” was the glorious chant raining down from the Hull support after Liam Millar’s 82nd-minute strike.

The goal was a sucker punch for Coventry, who were pushing for a winner and looked set to claim at least their first point of the season. Frank Lampard, arms folded, was unmoved as the away end rejoiced.

He and Coventry may wonder where their first point – and, indeed, their first goal – will come from. Next is a daunting trip to Manchester City, before they host Brighton, who began the season with a 4-0 trouncing of Aston Villa. Hull, as they did last season, are exceeding all expectations.

Was losing to another promoted team, one who finished 22 points behind them last season, a mental blow? “It depends how much you want it to be,” Lampard said. “There are 36 games left; we’re two games in. It depends how you react to a defeat.”

For Coventry, as their owner and chair, Doug King, said beforehand, a first Premier League for more than 25 years was a historic day for the city. “I know how much it means to all of us,” he said, this also their first top-flight game in this stadium.

The buzz before kick-off was palpable, none more so than when King – wearing an elephant brooch on his suit, the animal that adorns Coventry’s badge and the city’s coat of arms – joined Coventry supporters in singing along to The Enemy’s We’ll Live and Die in These Towns, the club’s adopted prematch anthem. The pyrotechnics left a haze drifting across the pitch as things got under way.

At full time, it was down to Millar and Sergej Jakirovic, albeit after a little persuading, to conduct the Hull celebrations. “It gives us big confidence as a team, individuals, for me as well, because I don’t have experience at this level,” said Hull’s head coach. “We have a lot of work to do, we need to keep our feet on the ground and stay humble. We know our target: 38, 41 points? We will see.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Millar slots the ball away in the 82nd minute to win Hull the game. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Both teams lacked quality, but Coventry were undeniably the more threatening side. Taiwo Awoniyi, on his full league debut for the club, sent a weak header at Konstantinos Tzolakis and later forced the Hull goalkeeper into a smart right-hand save after Loum Tchaouna’s cross skidded off the head of Nobel Mendy. Lampard cycled through substitutions, the arrival of Gustavo Hamer, something of a hero in these parts, lifting the home crowd, but they struggled to work Tzolakis.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Millar, who arrived on the hour, had wasted Hull’s best opening with 74 minutes on the clock, Jakirovic wearing a look of disgust after the Canada winger ignored an unmarked Mohamed Belloumi to his right and sent his shot bobbling wide after a clever first-time pass by Oli McBurnie released Millar behind Bobby Thomas. Until then, their only shot on target was Mendy’s speculative shot from 30 yards.

But Millar made amends, coolly slotting past Carl Rushworth to cap a devastating counterattack. Victor Torp’s attempted cross from the left boomeranged off Lucas Gourna-Douath and into midfield, where Belloumi overpowered Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and sent Millar streaming into the opposition half with a sumptuous outside-of-the-boot pass.

“I think Millar was a bit disappointed with the first chance but then showed massive bollocks to score the second,” McBurnie said. “As a striker, it’s not the one you want when you’ve just missed a chance: you’ve got to run 40 yards and then think about your shot. You’ve got too much time to think.”

Twelve months ago, Hull were reeling from back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Bristol City and adapting to life under a transfer embargo. They made up for lost time this summer with Mohamed Ali-Cho, who made his debut late on here, and another forward, Ilyas Ansah, a £20m buy from Union Berlin, their 12th and 13th arrivals of the window respectively.

“We knew this was going to be a really tough game, in some ways even tougher than last week,” McBurnie said. “Considering we’re ‘the worst team in Premier League history’, it’s not a bad start from the boys.”

Sports.title: Amin Nabizada sparkles for Watford as draw puts pressure on West Ham’s Nuno
Sports.content:
When a club is an established part of English football’s upper echelons, plays its home games inside a 68,000-seater stadium, and promptly breaks the Championship transfer record following relegation from the top flight, there are expectations that naturally follow. By all accounts, West Ham were supposed to breeze through what is only meant to be a brief dalliance with a second-tier existence. To be winless three league matches into the season was inconceivable.

If the travelling contingent’s boos after this draw at Watford were fleeting, their subsequent burst of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” directed at their team’s manager left no ambiguity. No matter how embryonic this campaign is, the repeated impotency is already unacceptable, and now Nuno Espírito Santo is in the firing line.

A 46-game Championship season is long and there remains abundant time to turn things around. But when you suggest that spending £22m on Arne Engels is with a view to him playing in the Premier League – as Nuno did earlier this summer – you leave yourself little wriggle room when things do not follow the expectedly smooth course.

“We are a big club, we are favourites to go up,” said Nuno. “We have three games, we have two points. Who is happy? But me? I believe. I trust my boys. I work very hard with them. We are building a team. Things will change. I am positive.

“The fans are the most important part of our club and I respect them so much. I understand everything. I just ask again to keep believing, keep trusting us, keep going and we will try to reverse it. The win must come, hopefully on Tuesday [against fellow relegated side Wolves]. We need it.”

That this draw – which followed another against Burnley and defeat to Charlton – came against a Watford team openly treading water only emphasised West Ham’s struggles.
